# gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/

## Expand description

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for **GTK 3**, part of [gtk3-rs](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs),
a multi-platform GUI toolkit. It is a part of [gtk-rs](http://gtk-rs.org/).

GTK **3.18** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.56.0`.

**gtk** expects **GTK**, **GLib** and **Cairo** development files to be installed on your system.
See the [GTK installation page](https://www.gtk.org/docs/installations/).

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](http://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
gtk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
[dependencies]
gtk = "0.13"
gtk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git" }
```
//!
GTK needs to be initialized before use by calling [ init](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html). Creating an

[will call](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html)

`Application`[for you.](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init````
use gtk::prelude::*;
use gtk::{Application, ApplicationWindow};
fn main() {
    let app = Application::builder()
        .application_id("org.example.HelloWorld")
        .build();
    app.connect_activate(|app| {
        // We create the main window.
        let win = ApplicationWindow::builder()
            .application(app)
            .default_width(320)
            .default_height(200)
            .title("Hello, World!")
            .build();
        // Don't forget to make all widgets visible.
        win.show_all();
    });
    app.run();
}
```
In a typical GTK application you set up the UI, assign signal handlers and run the main event loop.

```
use gtk::prelude::*;
use gtk::{Application, ApplicationWindow, Button};
fn main() {
    let application = Application::builder()
        .application_id("com.example.FirstGtkApp")
        .build();
    application.connect_activate(|app| {
        let window = ApplicationWindow::builder()
            .application(app)
            .title("First GTK Program")
            .default_width(350)
            .default_height(70)
            .build();
        let button = Button::with_label("Click me!");
        button.connect_clicked(|_| {
            eprintln!("Clicked!");
        });
        window.add(&button);
        window.show_all();
    });
    application.run();
}
```
GTK is not thread-safe. Accordingly, none of this crate’s structs implement
[ Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) or

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)

`Sync`The thread where [ init](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html) was called is considered the main thread. OS X has
its own notion of the main thread and

[must be called on that thread. After successful initialization, calling any](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init`[or](https://gtk-rs.org/index.html)

`gtk`[functions (including](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/index.html)

`gdk`[) from other threads will](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init``panic`.Any thread can schedule a closure to be run by the main loop on the main
thread via [ glib::idle_add](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.idle_add.html) or

[. While working with GTK you might need the](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.timeout_add.html)

`glib::timeout_add`[or](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.idle_add_local.html)

`glib::idle_add_local`[version without the](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.timeout_add_local.html)

`glib::timeout_add_local`[bound. Those may only be called from the main thread.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)

`Send`The [ gtk](https://gtk-rs.org/index.html) and

[crates have some run-time safety and contract checks.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/index.html)

`gdk`-
Any constructor or free function will panic if called before `init`
-
Any `&str``&Path``\0`) character will cause a panic.
-
Some functions will panic if supplied out-of-range integer parameters. All such cases will be documented individually but they are not yet.
-
A panic in a closure that handles signals or in any other closure passed to a `gtk`

By default this crate provides only GTK 3.18 APIs. You can access additional
functionality by selecting one of the `v3_20`, `v3_24`, etc. features.

`Cargo.toml` example:

```
[dependencies.gtk]
version = "0.x.y"
features = ["v3_20"]
```
Take care when choosing the version to target: some of your users might not have easy access to the latest ones. The higher the version, the fewer users will have it installed.

Most of this documentation is generated from the C API.

Until all parts of the documentation have been reviewed there will be incongruities with the actual Rust API.

Generate the docs:

`> cargo doc --features dox`(if the installed GTK+ version is lower than 3.16, adjust the feature name accordingly).

Contributor you’re welcome!

See the general [bindings documentation](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/).

Most of the bindings ([ src/auto](https://gtk-rs.org/src/auto)) are generated by

[gir](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gir)using

[this configuration file](https://gtk-rs.org/Gir.toml). After editing

`Gir.toml` the sources can be regenerated with`> make gir`When opening a PR please put the changes to the `src/auto` directory in a separate commit.

You may also wish to run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and check that you’re clean because
otherwise you may be surprised when CI fails.

But also:

**gtk** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

The GtkAboutDialog offers a simple way to display information about
a program like its logo, name, copyright, website and license. It is
also possible to give credits to the authors, documenters, translators
and artists who have worked on the program. An about dialog is typically
opened when the user selects the `About` option from the `Help` menu.
All parts of the dialog are optional.

the `property::Widget::halign` and `property::Widget::valign` properties can be used on
the children to influence their allocation.

A GtkComboBox is a widget that allows the user to choose from a list of valid choices. The GtkComboBox displays the selected choice. When activated, the GtkComboBox displays a popup which allows the user to make a new choice. The style in which the selected value is displayed, and the style of the popup is determined by the current theme. It may be similar to a Windows-style combo box.

A GTK+ user interface is constructed by nesting widgets inside widgets.

they contain other widgets. So, for example, you might have a [ Window](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Window.html)
containing a

[containing a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Frame.html)

`Frame`[. If you wanted an image instead of a textual label inside the frame, you might replace the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Label.html)

`Label`[widget.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Image.html)

GtkHeaderBar is similar to a horizontal [ Box](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Box.html). It allows children to
be placed at the start or the end. In addition, it allows a title and
subtitle to be displayed. The title will be centered with respect to

# gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/index.html

## Expand description

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for **GTK 3**, part of [gtk3-rs](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs),
a multi-platform GUI toolkit. It is a part of [gtk-rs](http://gtk-rs.org/).

GTK **3.18** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.56.0`.

**gtk** expects **GTK**, **GLib** and **Cairo** development files to be installed on your system.
See the [GTK installation page](https://www.gtk.org/docs/installations/).

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](http://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
gtk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
[dependencies]
gtk = "0.13"
gtk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git" }
```
//!
GTK needs to be initialized before use by calling [ init](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html). Creating an

[will call](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html)

`Application`[for you.](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init````
use gtk::prelude::*;
use gtk::{Application, ApplicationWindow};
fn main() {
    let app = Application::builder()
        .application_id("org.example.HelloWorld")
        .build();
    app.connect_activate(|app| {
        // We create the main window.
        let win = ApplicationWindow::builder()
            .application(app)
            .default_width(320)
            .default_height(200)
            .title("Hello, World!")
            .build();
        // Don't forget to make all widgets visible.
        win.show_all();
    });
    app.run();
}
```
In a typical GTK application you set up the UI, assign signal handlers and run the main event loop.

```
use gtk::prelude::*;
use gtk::{Application, ApplicationWindow, Button};
fn main() {
    let application = Application::builder()
        .application_id("com.example.FirstGtkApp")
        .build();
    application.connect_activate(|app| {
        let window = ApplicationWindow::builder()
            .application(app)
            .title("First GTK Program")
            .default_width(350)
            .default_height(70)
            .build();
        let button = Button::with_label("Click me!");
        button.connect_clicked(|_| {
            eprintln!("Clicked!");
        });
        window.add(&button);
        window.show_all();
    });
    application.run();
}
```
GTK is not thread-safe. Accordingly, none of this crate’s structs implement
[ Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) or

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)

`Sync`The thread where [ init](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html) was called is considered the main thread. OS X has
its own notion of the main thread and

[must be called on that thread. After successful initialization, calling any](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init`[or](https://gtk-rs.org/index.html)

`gtk`[functions (including](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/index.html)

`gdk`[) from other threads will](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init``panic`.Any thread can schedule a closure to be run by the main loop on the main
thread via [ glib::idle_add](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.idle_add.html) or

[. While working with GTK you might need the](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.timeout_add.html)

`glib::timeout_add`[or](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.idle_add_local.html)

`glib::idle_add_local`[version without the](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.timeout_add_local.html)

`glib::timeout_add_local`[bound. Those may only be called from the main thread.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)

`Send`The [ gtk](https://gtk-rs.org/index.html) and

[crates have some run-time safety and contract checks.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/index.html)

`gdk`-
Any constructor or free function will panic if called before `init`
-
Any `&str``&Path``\0`) character will cause a panic.
-
Some functions will panic if supplied out-of-range integer parameters. All such cases will be documented individually but they are not yet.
-
A panic in a closure that handles signals or in any other closure passed to a `gtk`

By default this crate provides only GTK 3.18 APIs. You can access additional
functionality by selecting one of the `v3_20`, `v3_24`, etc. features.

`Cargo.toml` example:

```
[dependencies.gtk]
version = "0.x.y"
features = ["v3_20"]
```
Take care when choosing the version to target: some of your users might not have easy access to the latest ones. The higher the version, the fewer users will have it installed.

Most of this documentation is generated from the C API.

Until all parts of the documentation have been reviewed there will be incongruities with the actual Rust API.

Generate the docs:

`> cargo doc --features dox`(if the installed GTK+ version is lower than 3.16, adjust the feature name accordingly).

Contributor you’re welcome!

See the general [bindings documentation](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/).

Most of the bindings ([ src/auto](https://gtk-rs.org/src/auto)) are generated by

[gir](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gir)using

[this configuration file](https://gtk-rs.org/Gir.toml). After editing

`Gir.toml` the sources can be regenerated with`> make gir`When opening a PR please put the changes to the `src/auto` directory in a separate commit.

You may also wish to run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and check that you’re clean because
otherwise you may be surprised when CI fails.

But also:

**gtk** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

# Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust – gtk-rs

Source: http://gtk-rs.org/

#

          Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust [§](http://gtk-rs.org#unlocking-the-gnome-stack-for-rust)

The **gtk-rs** project provides safe bindings to the [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org) language for fundamental libraries from the [GNOME](https://developer.gnome.org/components/) stack like [GLib](https://developer.gnome.org/glib), [Cairo](https://cairographics.org/documentation/), and [GTK 4](https://gtk.org).

##

          Available crates [§](http://gtk-rs.org#available-crates)

The following table contains the most popular crates of **gtk-rs**. More information on all existing crates is available under the corresponding links in the **Project** column in the table below.

##

          The introductory book [§](http://gtk-rs.org#the-introductory-book)

  Julian Hofer is writing a book titled [GUI development with Rust and GTK 4](http://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/book). We recommend both new and experienced **gtk-rs** users to have a look at it. While this book is targeted at people who want to develop GTK 4 applications, it also covers more general aspects of the GNOME stack such as **GObject Concepts**, **The Main Event Loop** and **GSettings**.

##

          The gtk-rs ecosystem [§](http://gtk-rs.org#the-gtk-rs-ecosystem)

By now, a number of additional bindings for GObject based libraries exist. While not part of the gtk-rs project, many of them are developed in close collaboration. Notable other projects within the gtk-rs ecosystem are

- **GStreamer**Open source multimedia framework
- **Adwaita**Building blocks for modern GNOME applications
- **SourceView 5**A library extending GtkTextView with features typical for a source code editor
- **Relm 4**An idiomatic GUI library inspired by Elm and based on gtk4-rs

More bindings can be found as part of the [GNOME GitLab Rust Group](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Rust).

All these bindings are generated on the basis of GObject introspection (GIR). The book [Generate Rust bindings for GIR based libraries](http://gtk-rs.org/gir/book/) provides the documentation for the tools that gtk-rs provides to generate such bindings.

##

          Apps built with gtk-rs [§](http://gtk-rs.org#apps-built-with-gtk-rs)

# init in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/fn.init.html

## Expand description

Tries to initialize GTK+.

Call either this function or [ Application::new](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html#method.new) before using any
other GTK+ functions.

Note that this function calls `gtk_init_check()` rather than `gtk_init()`,
so will not cause the program to terminate if GTK could not be initialized.
Instead, an Ok is returned if the windowing system was successfully
initialized otherwise an Err is returned.

# Application in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Application.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Application { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ Application](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html) is a class that handles many important aspects
of a GTK+ application in a convenient fashion, without enforcing
a one-size-fits-all application model.

Currently, GtkApplication handles GTK+ initialization, application uniqueness, session management, provides some basic scriptability and desktop shell integration by exporting actions and menus and manages a list of toplevel windows whose life-cycle is automatically tied to the life-cycle of your application.

While GtkApplication works fine with plain `GtkWindows`, it is recommended
to use it together with [ ApplicationWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ApplicationWindow.html).

When GDK threads are enabled, GtkApplication will acquire the GDK
lock when invoking actions that arrive from other processes. The GDK
lock is not touched for local action invocations. In order to have
actions invoked in a predictable context it is therefore recommended
that the GDK lock be held while invoking actions locally with
[`ActionGroupExtManual::activate_action()`][crate::gio::prelude::ActionGroupExtManual::activate_action()]. The same applies to actions
associated with [ ApplicationWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ApplicationWindow.html) and to the “activate” and
“open”

[methods.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/application/struct.Application.html)

`gio::Application`[ Application](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html) will automatically load menus from the

[resource located at “gtk/menus.ui”, relative to the application’s resource base path (see [](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Builder.html)

`Builder``ApplicationExtManual::set_resource_base_path()`][crate::gio::prelude::ApplicationExtManual::set_resource_base_path()]). The
menu with the ID “app-menu” is taken as the application’s app menu
and the menu with the ID “menubar” is taken as the application’s
menubar. Additional menus (most interesting submenus) can be named
and accessed via [which allows for dynamic population of a part of the menu structure.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkApplicationExt.html#tymethod.menu_by_id)

`GtkApplicationExt::menu_by_id()`If the resources “gtk/menus-appmenu.ui” or “gtk/menus-traditional.ui” are
present then these files will be used in preference, depending on the value
of [ GtkApplicationExt::prefers_app_menu()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkApplicationExt.html#tymethod.prefers_app_menu). If the resource “gtk/menus-common.ui”
is present it will be loaded as well. This is useful for storing items that
are referenced from both “gtk/menus-appmenu.ui” and
“gtk/menus-traditional.ui”.

It is also possible to provide the menus manually using
[ GtkApplicationExt::set_app_menu()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkApplicationExt.html#tymethod.set_app_menu) and

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkApplicationExt.html#tymethod.set_menubar)

`GtkApplicationExt::set_menubar()`[ Application](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html) will also automatically setup an icon search path for
the default icon theme by appending “icons” to the resource base
path. This allows your application to easily store its icons as
resources. See

[for more information.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.IconThemeExt.html#tymethod.add_resource_path)

`IconThemeExt::add_resource_path()`If there is a resource located at “gtk/help-overlay.ui” which
defines a [ ShortcutsWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ShortcutsWindow.html) with ID “help_overlay” then GtkApplication
associates an instance of this shortcuts window with each

[and sets up keyboard accelerators (Control-F1 and Control-?) to open it. To create a menu item that displays the shortcuts window, associate the item with the action win.show-help-overlay.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ApplicationWindow.html)

`ApplicationWindow`GtkApplication optionally registers with a session manager
of the users session (if you set the `property::Application::register-session`
property) and offers various functionality related to the session
life-cycle.

An application can block various ways to end the session with
the [ GtkApplicationExt::inhibit()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkApplicationExt.html#tymethod.inhibit) function. Typical use cases for
this kind of inhibiting are long-running, uninterruptible operations,
such as burning a CD or performing a disk backup. The session
manager may not honor the inhibitor, but it can be expected to
inform the user about the negative consequences of ending the
session while inhibitors are present.

[HowDoI: Using GtkApplication](https://wiki.gnome.org/HowDoI/GtkApplication),
[Getting Started with GTK+: Basics](https://developer.gnome.org/gtk3/stable/gtk-getting-started.html%60id%60-1.2.3.3)

[ GtkApplicationExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkApplicationExt.html),

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/application/trait.ApplicationExt.html)

`gio::prelude::ApplicationExt`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/object/trait.ObjectExt.html)

`glib::ObjectExt`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/action_group/trait.ActionGroupExt.html)

`gio::prelude::ActionGroupExt`[, [](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/action_map/trait.ActionMapExt.html)

`gio::prelude::ActionMapExt``gio::ApplicationExtManual`][trait@crate::prelude::gio::ApplicationExtManual][source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gtk/subclass/application.rs.html#63-108)### impl<T: [GtkApplicationImpl](https://gtk-rs.org/subclass/application/trait.GtkApplicationImpl.html)> [IsSubclassable](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/subclass/types/trait.IsSubclassable.html)<T> for [Application](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html)

# gdk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gdk/index.html

## Expand description

Project site is [here](https://gtk-rs.org/).

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GDK 3](https://developer.gnome.org/gdk3/),
part of [gtk3-rs](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs).

GDK **3.18** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.56.0`.

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
gdk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git", package = "gdk" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
[dependencies]
gdk = "0.13"
gdk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git", package = "gdk" }
```
**gdk** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

GdkAppLaunchContext is an implementation of [ gio::AppLaunchContext](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/app_launch_context/struct.AppLaunchContext.html) that
handles launching an application in a graphical context. It provides
startup notification and allows to launch applications on a specific
screen or workspace.

In addition to a single pointer and keyboard for user interface input, GDK contains support for a variety of input devices, including graphics tablets, touchscreens and multiple pointers/keyboards interacting simultaneously with the user interface. Such input devices often have additional features, such as sub-pixel positioning information and additional device-dependent information.

Used for button press and button release events. The

# idle_add in glib::source - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.idle_add.html

## Expand description

Adds a closure to be called by the default main loop when it’s idle.

`func` will be called repeatedly until it returns `Continue(false)`.

The default main loop almost always is the main loop of the main thread. Thus, the closure is called on the main thread.

---

# timeout_add in glib::source - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.timeout_add.html

`pub fn timeout_add<F>(interval: `[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html), func: F) -> [SourceId](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.SourceId.html)where
    F: [FnMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnMut.html)() -> [Continue](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Continue.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'static,## Expand description

Adds a closure to be called by the default main loop at regular intervals with millisecond granularity.

`func` will be called repeatedly every `interval` milliseconds until it
returns `Continue(false)`. Precise timing is not guaranteed, the timeout may
be delayed by other events. Prefer `timeout_add_seconds` when millisecond
precision is not necessary.

The default main loop almost always is the main loop of the main thread. Thus, the closure is called on the main thread.

---

# idle_add_local in glib::source - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/source/fn.idle_add_local.html

## Expand description

Adds a closure to be called by the default main loop when it’s idle.

`func` will be called repeatedly until it returns `Continue(false)`.

The default main loop almost always is the main loop of the main thread. Thus, the closure is called on the main thread.

Different to `idle_add()`, this does not require `func` to be
`Send` but can only be called from the thread that owns the main context.

This function panics if called from a different thread than the one that owns the default main context.

---

# gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/git/docs/gtk

## Expand description

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for **GTK 3**, part of [gtk3-rs](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs),
a multi-platform GUI toolkit. It is a part of [gtk-rs](http://gtk-rs.org/).

GTK **3.22.30** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.63.0`.

**gtk** expects **GTK**, **GLib** and **Cairo** development files to be installed on your system.
See the [GTK installation page](https://www.gtk.org/docs/installations/).

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](http://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
gtk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
[dependencies]
gtk = "0.13"
gtk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git" }
```
//!
GTK needs to be initialized before use by calling [ init](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html). Creating an

[will call](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Application.html)

`Application`[for you.](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.init.html)

`init````
use gtk::prelude::*;
use gtk::{Application, ApplicationWindow};
fn main() {
    let app = Application::builder()
        .application_id("org.example.HelloWorld")
        .build();
    app.connect_activate(|app| {
        // We create the main window.
        let win = ApplicationWindow::builder()
            .application(app)
            .default_width(320)
            .default_height(200)
            .title("Hello, World!")
            .build();
        // Don't forget to make all widgets visible.
        win.show_all();
    });
    app.run();
}
```
In a typical GTK application you set up the UI, assign signal handlers and run the main event loop.

```
use gtk::prelude::*;
use gtk::{Application, ApplicationWindow, Button};
fn main() {
    let application = Application::builder()
        .application_id("com.example.FirstGtkApp")
        .build();
    application.connect_activate(|app| {
        let window = ApplicationWindow::builder()
            .application(app)
            .title("First GTK Program")
            .default_width(350)
            .default_height(70)
            .build();
        let button = Button::with_label("Click me!");
        button.connect_clicked(|_| {
            eprintln!("Clicked!");
        });
        window.add(&button);
        window.show_all();
    });
    application.run();
}
```

By default this crate provides only GTK 3.22.30 APIs. You can access additional
functionality by selecting one of the `v3_24`, etc. features.

`Cargo.toml` example:

```
[dependencies.gtk]
version = "0.x.y"
features = ["v3_24"]
```
Take care when choosing the version to target: some of your users might not have easy access to the latest ones. The higher the version, the fewer users will have it installed.

Most of this documentation is generated from the C API.

Until all parts of the documentation have been reviewed there will be incongruities with the actual Rust API.

Generate the docs:

`> cargo doc --features dox`(if the installed GTK+ version is lower than 3.16, adjust the feature name accordingly).

# glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-glib-and-gobject-bindings)Rust GLib and GObject bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GLib](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GLib **2.56** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

This library contains bindings to GLib and GObject types and APIs as well as common building blocks used in both handmade and machine generated bindings to GTK and other GLib-based libraries.

It is the foundation for higher level libraries with uniform Rusty (safe and strongly typed) APIs. It avoids exposing GLib-specific data types where possible and is not meant to provide comprehensive GLib bindings, which would often amount to duplicating the Rust Standard Library or other utility crates.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dynamic-typing)Dynamic typing

Most types in the GLib family have [ Type](https://gtk-rs.org/types/struct.Type.html) identifiers.
Their corresponding Rust types implement the

[trait.](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)

`StaticType`A dynamically typed [ Value](https://gtk-rs.org/value/struct.Value.html) can carry values of any

`StaticType`.
[Variants](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/variant/struct.Variant.html)can carry values of

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/variant/trait.StaticVariantType.html)

`StaticVariantType`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#errors)Errors

Errors are represented by [ Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html), which can
carry values from various

[error domains](https://gtk-rs.org/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)such as

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)

`FileError`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#objects)Objects

Each class and interface has a corresponding smart pointer struct
representing an instance of that type (e.g. [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) for

[or](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html)

`GObject`[for](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/struct.Widget.html)

`gtk4::Widget`[). They are reference counted and feature interior mutability similarly to Rust’s](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html)

`GtkWidget`[idiom. Consequently, cloning objects is cheap and their methods never require mutable borrows. Two smart pointers are equal if they point to the same object.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/index.html#introducing-mutability-inside-of-something-immutable)

`Rc<RefCell<T>>`The root of the object hierarchy is [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html).
Inheritance and subtyping is denoted with the

[marker trait. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.IsA.html)

`IsA`[trait enables upcasting and downcasting.](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.Cast.html)

`Cast`Interfaces and non-leaf classes also have corresponding traits (e.g.
[ ObjectExt](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.ObjectExt.html) or

[), which are blanketly implemented for all their subtypes.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/prelude/trait.WidgetExt.html)

`WidgetExt`You can create new subclasses of [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) or other object types. Look at
the module’s documentation for further details and a code example.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#under-the-hood)Under the hood

GLib-based libraries largely operate on pointers to various boxed or
reference counted structures so the bindings have to implement corresponding
smart pointers (wrappers), which encapsulate resource management and safety
checks. Such wrappers are defined via the
[ wrapper!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.wrapper.html) macro, which uses abstractions
defined in the

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/wrapper/index.html)

`wrapper`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/boxed/index.html)

`boxed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/shared/index.html)

`shared`[modules. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/index.html)

`object`[module defines and partly implements conversions between high level Rust types (including the aforementioned wrappers) and their FFI counterparts.](https://gtk-rs.org/translate/index.html)

`translate`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
glib = "0.13"
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**glib** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- [CvtError](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.CvtError.html)
- A wrapper for `ConvertError`
- [Date](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.DateMonth.html)- Month
- Enumeration representing a month; values are `January``February``BadMonth`
- [Date](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.DateWeekday.html)- Weekday
- Enumeration representing a day of the week; `Monday``Tuesday``BadWeekday`
- [Decomposition](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.DecompositionKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of decomposition to perform
- [File](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)- Error
- Values corresponding to @errno codes returned from file operations on UNIX. Unlike @errno codes, GFileError values are available on all systems, even Windows. The exact meaning of each code depends on what sort of file operation you were performing; the UNIX documentation gives more details. The following error code descriptions come from the GNU C Library manual, and are under the copyright of that manual.
- [GStr](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.GStrError.html)- Error
- Error type holding all possible failures when creating a `GStr`
- [GString](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.GStringFromError.html)- From - Error
- Error type holding all possible failures when creating a `GString`
- [Glib](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.GlibLoggerDomain.html)- Logger - Domain - `log`
- Enumeration of the possible domain handling behaviours for a
`GlibLogger`
- [Glib](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.GlibLoggerFormat.html)- Logger - Format - `log`
- Enumeration of the possible formatting behaviours for a
`GlibLogger`
- [IConv](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.IConvError.html)- Error
- A wrapper for `std::io::Error`
- [KeyFile](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.KeyFileError.html)- Error
- Error codes returned by key file parsing.
- [LogLevel](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogLevel.html)
- [LogWriter](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogWriterOutput.html)- Output
- Return values from #GLogWriterFuncs to indicate whether the given log entry was successfully handled by the writer, or whether there was an error in handling it (and hence a fallback writer should be used).
- [Markup](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.MarkupError.html)- Error
- Error codes returned by markup parsing.
- [Normalize](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.NormalizeMode.html)- Mode
- Defines how a Unicode string is transformed in a canonical form, standardizing such issues as whether a character with an accent is represented as a base character and combining accent or as a single precomposed character. Unicode strings should generally be normalized before comparing them.
- [Option](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.OptionArg.html)- Arg
- The #GOptionArg enum values determine which type of extra argument the
options expect to find. If an option expects an extra argument, it can
be specified in several ways; with a short option: `-x arg`, with a long option:`--name arg`or combined in a single argument:`--name=arg`.
- [Seek](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.SeekType.html)- Type
- An enumeration specifying the base position for a g_io_channel_seek_position() operation.
- [Time](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TimeType.html)- Type
- Disambiguates a given time in two ways.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeBreakType.html)- Break - Type
- These are the possible line break classifications.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeScript.html)- Script
- The #GUnicodeScript enumeration identifies different writing systems. The values correspond to the names as defined in the Unicode standard. The enumeration has been added in GLib 2.14, and is interchangeable with #PangoScript.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeType.html)- Type
- These are the possible character classifications from the
Unicode specification.
See [Unicode Character Database](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr44/#General_Category_Values).
- [UriError](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UriError.html)- `v2_66`
- Error codes returned by #GUri methods.
- [Variant](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.VariantClass.html)- Class
- The range of possible top-level types of #GVariant instances.

- [CSET_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.CSET_A_2_Z.html)- A_ - 2_ - Z

[Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/).
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ACTIONS.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ACTIONS
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string list giving the available application actions.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_CATEGORIES.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - CATEGORIES
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings giving the categories in which the desktop entry should be shown in a menu.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_COMMENT.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - COMMENT
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the tooltip for the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_DBUS_ACTIVATABLE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - DBUS_ - ACTIVATABLE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean set to true if the application is D-Bus activatable.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_EXEC.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - EXEC
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the command line to execute.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_GENERIC_NAME.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - GENERIC_ - NAME
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the generic name of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_HIDDEN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - HIDDEN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the desktop entry has been deleted by the user.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ICON.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ICON
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the name of the icon to be displayed for the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_MIME_TYPE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - MIME_ - TYPE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings giving the MIME types supported by this desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_NAME.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - NAME
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the specific name of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_NOT_SHOW_IN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - NOT_ - SHOW_ - IN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings identifying the environments that should not display the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_NO_DISPLAY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - NO_ - DISPLAY
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the desktop entry should be shown in menus.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ONLY_SHOW_IN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ONLY_ - SHOW_ - IN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings identifying the environments that should display the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_PATH.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - PATH
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string containing the working directory to run the program in.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_STARTUP_NOTIFY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - STARTUP_ - NOTIFY
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the application supports the[Startup Notification Protocol Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/startup-notification-spec/latest/).
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_STARTUP_WM_CLASS.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - STARTUP_ - WM_ - CLASS
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is string identifying the WM class or name hint of a window that the application will create, which can be used to emulate[Startup Notification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/startup-notification-spec/latest/)with older applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TERMINAL.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TERMINAL
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the program should be run in a terminal window.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TRY_EXEC.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TRY_ - EXEC
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the file name of a binary on disk used to determine if the program is actually installed.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TYPE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the type of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_URL.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - URL
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the URL to access.

- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the version of the Desktop Entry Specification used for the desktop entry file.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_APPLICATION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - APPLICATION
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_DIRECTORY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - DIRECTORY
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing directories.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_LINK.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - LINK
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing links to documents.
- [OPTION_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.OPTION_REMAINING.html)- REMAINING
- If a long option in the main group has this name, it is not treated as a
regular option. Instead it collects all non-option arguments which would
otherwise be left in `argv`. The option must be of type`OptionArg::Callback``OptionArg::StringArray``OptionArg::FilenameArray`
- [STR_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.STR_DELIMITERS.html)- DELIMITERS
- The standard delimiters, used in `strdelimit()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_ISOLATE_DIRS.html)- OPTION_ - ISOLATE_ - DIRS - `v2_60`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.

- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NO_PRGNAME.html)- OPTION_ - NO_ - PRGNAME - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_GENERIC_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - GENERIC_ - DELIMITERS
- Generic delimiters characters as defined in

- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_SUBCOMPONENT_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - SUBCOMPONENT_ - DELIMITERS

## Functions[§](https://gtk-rs.org#functions)

- [access](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.access.html)
- A wrapper for the POSIX access() function. This function is used to test a pathname for one or several of read, write or execute permissions, or just existence.
- [application_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.application_name.html)- name
- Gets a human-readable name for the application, as set by
g_set_application_name(). This name should be localized if
possible, and is intended for display to the user.  Contrast with
g_get_prgname(), which gets a non-localized name. If
g_set_application_name() has not been called, returns the result of
g_get_prgname() (which may be `None`
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_decode.html)- decode
- Decode a sequence of Base-64 encoded text into binary data. Note that the returned binary data is not necessarily zero-terminated, so it should not be used as a character string.
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_encode.html)- encode
- Encode a sequence of binary data into its Base-64 stringified representation.
- [casefold](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.casefold.html)
- [charset](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.charset.html)
- Obtain the character set for the current locale.
- [check_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.check_version.html)- version
- Checks that the GLib library in use is compatible with the given version.
- [child_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.child_watch_future.html)- watch_ - future - `futures`
- Create a `Future`that will resolve once the child process with the given pid exits
- [child_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.child_watch_future_with_priority.html)- watch_ - future_ - with_ - priority - `futures`
- Create a `Future`that will resolve once the child process with the given pid exits
- [codeset](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.codeset.html)
- Gets the character set for the current locale.
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_bytes.html)- checksum_ - for_ - bytes
- Computes the checksum for a binary @data. This is a convenience wrapper for g_checksum_new(), g_checksum_get_string() and g_checksum_free().
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_data.html)- checksum_ - for_ - data
- Computes the checksum for a binary @data of @length. This is a convenience wrapper for g_checksum_new(), g_checksum_get_string() and g_checksum_free().
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_string.html)- checksum_ - for_ - string
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_hmac_for_bytes.html)- hmac_ - for_ - bytes
- Computes the HMAC for a binary @data. This is a convenience wrapper for g_hmac_new(), g_hmac_get_string() and g_hmac_unref().
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_hmac_for_data.html)- hmac_ - for_ - data
- Computes the HMAC for a binary @data of @length. This is a convenience wrapper for g_hmac_new(), g_hmac_get_string() and g_hmac_unref().
- [console_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.console_charset.html)- charset - `v2_62`
- Obtains the character set used by the console attached to the process, which is suitable for printing output to the terminal.
- [convert](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert.html)
- Converts a string from one character set to another.
- [convert_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert_with_fallback.html)- with_ - fallback
- Converts a string from one character set to another, possibly including fallback sequences for characters not representable in the output. Note that it is not guaranteed that the specification for the fallback sequences in @fallback will be honored. Some systems may do an approximate conversion from @from_codeset to @to_codeset in their iconv() functions, in which case GLib will simply return that approximate conversion.
- [current_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.current_dir.html)- dir
- Gets the current directory.
- [dcgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dcgettext.html)
- This is a variant of g_dgettext() that allows specifying a locale
category instead of always using `LC_MESSAGES`. See g_dgettext() for more information about how this functions differs from calling dcgettext() directly.
- [dgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dgettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dgettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dngettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dngettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dngettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dpgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid. If 0 is passed as @msgidoffset, this function will fall back to trying to use the deprecated convention of using “|” as a separation character.
- [dpgettext2](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext2.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid.
- [environ](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ.html)
- Gets the list of environment variables for the current process.
- [environ_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ_getenv.html)- getenv
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_get_contents.html)- get_ - contents
- Reads an entire file into allocated memory, with good error checking.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_open_tmp.html)- open_ - tmp - Unix
- Opens a file for writing in the preferred directory for temporary files (as returned by g_get_tmp_dir()).
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents.html)- set_ - contents
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename. This is a convenience
wrapper around calling g_file_set_contents_full() with `flags`set to`G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_CONSISTENT | G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_ONLY_EXISTING`and`mode`set to`0666`.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents_full.html)- set_ - contents_ - full - `v2_66`
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename, with good error checking. If a file called @filename already exists it will be overwritten.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_charsets.html)- charsets
- Determines the preferred character sets used for filenames. The first character set from the @charsets is the filename encoding, the subsequent character sets are used when trying to generate a displayable representation of a filename, see g_filename_display_name().
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_basename.html)- display_ - basename
- Returns the display basename for the particular filename, guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. The display name might not be identical to the filename, for instance there might be problems converting it to UTF-8, and some files can be translated in the display.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_name.html)- display_ - name
- Converts a filename into a valid UTF-8 string. The conversion is
not necessarily reversible, so you should keep the original around
and use the return value of this function only for display purposes.
Unlike g_filename_to_utf8(), the result is guaranteed to be non-`None`
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_uri.html)- from_ - uri
- Converts an escaped ASCII-encoded URI to a local filename in the encoding used for filenames.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_utf8.html)- from_ - utf8
- Converts a string from UTF-8 to the encoding GLib uses for
filenames. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8 for filenames;
on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on the
[current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_uri.html)- to_ - uri
- Converts an absolute filename to an escaped ASCII-encoded URI, with the path component following Section 3.3. of RFC 2396.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_utf8.html)- to_ - utf8
- Converts a string which is in the encoding used by GLib for
filenames into a UTF-8 string. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8
for filenames; on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on
the [current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [find_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.find_program_in_path.html)- program_ - in_ - path
- Locates the first executable named @program in the user’s path, in the
same way that execvp() would locate it. Returns an allocated string
with the absolute path name, or `None``None`
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size.html)- size
- Formats a size (for example the size of a file) into a human readable string. Sizes are rounded to the nearest size prefix (kB, MB, GB) and are displayed rounded to the nearest tenth. E.g. the file size 3292528 bytes will be converted into the string “3.2 MB”. The returned string is UTF-8, and may use a non-breaking space to separate the number and units, to ensure they aren’t separated when line wrapped.
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size_full.html)- size_ - full
- Formats a size.
- [future_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.future_with_timeout.html)- with_ - timeout - `futures`

- [future_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.future_with_timeout_with_priority.html)- with_ - timeout_ - with_ - priority - `futures`
- Add a timeout to a `Future`.

- Returns the value of an environment variable.

- [hostname_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.hostname_to_unicode.html)- to_ - unicode

# Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust – gtk-rs

Source: https://gtk-rs.org

#

          Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust [§](https://gtk-rs.org#unlocking-the-gnome-stack-for-rust)

The **gtk-rs** project provides safe bindings to the [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org) language for fundamental libraries from the [GNOME](https://developer.gnome.org/components/) stack like [GLib](https://developer.gnome.org/glib), [Cairo](https://cairographics.org/documentation/), and [GTK 4](https://gtk.org).

##

          Available crates [§](https://gtk-rs.org#available-crates)

The following table contains the most popular crates of **gtk-rs**. More information on all existing crates is available under the corresponding links in the **Project** column in the table below.

##

          The introductory book [§](https://gtk-rs.org#the-introductory-book)

  Julian Hofer is writing a book titled [GUI development with Rust and GTK 4](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/book). We recommend both new and experienced **gtk-rs** users to have a look at it. While this book is targeted at people who want to develop GTK 4 applications, it also covers more general aspects of the GNOME stack such as **GObject Concepts**, **The Main Event Loop** and **GSettings**.

##

          The gtk-rs ecosystem [§](https://gtk-rs.org#the-gtk-rs-ecosystem)

By now, a number of additional bindings for GObject based libraries exist. While not part of the gtk-rs project, many of them are developed in close collaboration. Notable other projects within the gtk-rs ecosystem are

- **GStreamer**Open source multimedia framework
- **Adwaita**Building blocks for modern GNOME applications
- **SourceView 5**A library extending GtkTextView with features typical for a source code editor
- **Relm 4**An idiomatic GUI library inspired by Elm and based on gtk4-rs

More bindings can be found as part of the [GNOME GitLab Rust Group](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Rust).

All these bindings are generated on the basis of GObject introspection (GIR). The book [Generate Rust bindings for GIR based libraries](https://gtk-rs.org/gir/book/) provides the documentation for the tools that gtk-rs provides to generate such bindings.

          Apps built with gtk-rs [§](https://gtk-rs.org#apps-built-with-gtk-rs)

# glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/index.html

## Expand description

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GLib](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GLib **2.48** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

This library contains bindings to GLib and GObject types and APIs as well as common building blocks used in both handmade and machine generated bindings to GTK and other GLib-based libraries.

It is the foundation for higher level libraries with uniform Rusty (safe and strongly typed) APIs. It avoids exposing GLib-specific data types where possible and is not meant to provide comprehensive GLib bindings, which would often amount to duplicating the Rust Standard Library or other utility crates.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.56.0`.

Most types in the GLib family have [ Type](https://gtk-rs.org/types/struct.Type.html) identifiers.
Their corresponding Rust types implement the

[trait.](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)

`StaticType`A dynamically typed [ Value](https://gtk-rs.org/value/struct.Value.html) can carry values of any

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)

`StaticType`[s can carry values of](https://gtk-rs.org/variant/struct.Variant.html)

`Variant`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/variant/trait.StaticVariantType.html)

`StaticVariantType`Errors are represented by [ Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html), which can
carry values from various

[error domains](https://gtk-rs.org/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)such as

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)

`FileError`Each class and interface has a corresponding smart pointer struct
representing an instance of that type (e.g. [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) for

`GObject` or
`gtk::Widget` for `GtkWidget`). They are reference counted and feature
interior mutability similarly to Rust’s `Rc<RefCell<T>>` idiom.
Consequently, cloning objects is cheap and their methods never require
mutable borrows. Two smart pointers are equal if they point to the same
object.The root of the object hierarchy is [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html).
Inheritance and subtyping is denoted with the

[marker trait. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.IsA.html)

`IsA`[trait enables upcasting and downcasting.](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.Cast.html)

`Cast`Interfaces and non-leaf classes also have corresponding traits (e.g.
[ ObjectExt](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.ObjectExt.html) or

`gtk::WidgetExt`), which are blanketly implemented for all
their subtypes.You can create new subclasses of [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) or other object types. Look at
the module’s documentation for further details and a code example.

GLib-based libraries largely operate on pointers to various boxed or
reference counted structures so the bindings have to implement corresponding
smart pointers (wrappers), which encapsulate resource management and safety
checks. Such wrappers are defined via the
[ wrapper](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.wrapper.html) macro, which uses abstractions
defined in the

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/wrapper/index.html)

`wrapper`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/boxed/index.html)

`boxed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/shared/index.html)

`shared`[modules.](https://gtk-rs.org/object/index.html)

`object`The [ translate](https://gtk-rs.org/translate/index.html) module defines and partly implements
conversions between high level Rust types (including the aforementioned
wrappers) and their FFI counterparts.

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
glib = "0.13"
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
**glib** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

# atk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/atk/index.html

## Expand description

Project site is [here](https://gtk-rs.org/).

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [ATK](https://developer.gnome.org/atk),
part of [gtk3-rs](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs).

ATK **2.18** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.56.0`.

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
atk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git", package = "atk" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
[dependencies]
atk = "0.13"
atk = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk3-rs.git", package = "atk" }
```
**atk** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

AtkAttribute is a string name/value pair representing a generic
attribute. This can be used to expose additional information from
an accessible object as a whole (see `atk_object_get_attributes()`)
or an document (see `atk_document_get_attributes()`). In the case of
text attributes (see `atk_text_get_default_attributes()`),
[ TextAttribute](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TextAttribute.html) enum defines all the possible text attribute
names. You can use

[to get the string name from the enum value. See also](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TextAttribute.html#method.name)

`TextAttribute::name()`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TextAttribute.html#method.for_name)

`TextAttribute::for_name()`[for more information.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TextAttribute.html#method.value)

`TextAttribute::value()`[ Component](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Component.html) should be implemented by most if not all UI elements
with an actual on-screen presence, i.e. components which can be
said to have a screen-coordinate bounding box. Virtually all
widgets will need to have

[implementations provided for their corresponding](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Component.html)

`Component`[class. In short, only UI elements which are](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Object.html)

`Object`*not*GUI elements will omit this ATK interface.

The AtkDocument interface should be supported by any object whose content is a representation or view of a document. The AtkDocument interface should appear on the toplevel container for the document content; however AtkDocument instances may be nested (i.e. an AtkDocument may be a descendant of another AtkDocument) in those cases where one document contains “embedded content” which can reasonably be considered a document in its own right.

This object class is derived from AtkObject. It can be used as a basis for implementing accessible objects for GObjects which are not derived from GtkWidget. One example of its use is in providing an accessible object for GnomeCanvasItem in the GAIL library.

An ATK object which encapsulates a link or set of links (for instance in the case of client-side image maps) in a hypertext document. It may implement the AtkAction interface. AtkHyperlink may also be used to refer to inline embedded content, since it allows specification of a start and end offset within the host AtkHypertext object.

AtkHyperlinkImpl allows AtkObjects to refer to their associated AtkHyperlink instance, if one exists. AtkHyperlinkImpl differs from AtkHyperlink in that AtkHyperlinkImpl is an interface, whereas AtkHyperlink is a object type. The AtkHyperlinkImpl interface allows a client to query an AtkObject for the availability of an associated AtkHyperlink instance, and obtain that instance. It is thus particularly useful in cases where embedded content or inline content within a text object is present, since the embedding text object implements AtkHypertext and the inline/embedded objects are exposed as children which implement AtkHyperlinkImpl, in addition to their being obtainable via AtkHypertext:getLink followed by AtkHyperlink:getObject.

An interface used for objects which implement linking between multiple resource or content locations, or multiple ‘markers’ within a single document. A Hypertext instance is associated with one or more Hyperlinks, which are associated with particular offsets within the Hypertext’s included content. While this interface is derived from Text, there is no requirement that Hypertext instances have textual content; they may implement Image as well, and Hyperlinks need not have non-zero text offsets.

[ Image](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Image.html) should be implemented by

[subtypes on behalf of components which display image/pixmap information onscreen, and which provide information (other than just widget borders, etc.) via that image content. For instance, icons, buttons with icons, toolbar elements, and image viewing panes typically should implement](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Object.html)

`Object`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Image.html)

`Image`A set of utility functions for thread locking. This interface and all his related methods are deprecated since 2.12.

An AtkNoOpObject is an AtkObject which purports to implement all ATK interfaces. It is the type of AtkObject which is created if an accessible object is requested for an object type for which no factory type is specified.

The AtkObjectFactory which creates an AtkNoOpObject. An instance of this is created by an AtkRegistry if no factory type has not been specified to create an accessible object of a particular type.

This class is the primary class for accessibility support via the
Accessibility ToolKit (ATK). Objects which are instances of
[ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Object.html) (or instances of AtkObject-derived types) are queried
for properties which relate basic (and generic) properties of a UI
component such as name and description. Instances of

[may also be queried as to whether they implement other ATK interfaces (e.g.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Object.html)

`Object`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Action.html)

`Action`[, etc.), as appropriate to the role which a given UI component plays in a user interface.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Component.html)

`Component`This class is the base object class for a factory used to create an
accessible object for a specific GType. The function
[ RegistryExt::set_factory_type()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.RegistryExt.html#tymethod.set_factory_type) is normally called to store in the
registry the factory type to be used to create an accessible of a
particular GType.

A data structure for holding a rectangle. Those coordinates are relative to the component top-level parent.

The AtkRegistry is normally used to create appropriate ATK “peers” for user interface components. Application developers usually need only interact with the AtkRegistry by associating appropriate ATK implementation classes with GObject classes via the atk_registry_set_factory_type call, passing the appropriate GType for application custom widget classes.

An AtkRelation describes a relation between an object and one or more other objects. The actual relations that an object has with other objects are defined as an AtkRelationSet, which is a set of AtkRelations.

The AtkRelationSet held by an object establishes its relationships with objects beyond the normal “parent/child” hierarchical relationships that all user interface objects have. AtkRelationSets establish whether objects are labelled or controlled by other components, share group membership with other components (for instance within a radio-button group), or share content which “flows” between them, among other types of possible relationships.

[ Selection](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Selection.html) should be implemented by UI components with children
which are exposed by

`atk_object_ref_child` and
`atk_object_get_n_children`, if the use of the parent UI component
ordinarily involves selection of one or more of the objects
corresponding to those [children - for example, selectable lists.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Object.html)

`Object`Together with [ Plug](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Plug.html),

[provides the ability to embed accessibles from one process into another in a fashion that is transparent to assistive technologies.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Socket.html)

`Socket`[works as the container of](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Socket.html)

`Socket`[, embedding it using the method](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Plug.html)

`Plug`[. Any accessible contained in the](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.AtkSocketExt.html#tymethod.embed)

`AtkSocketExt::embed()`[will appear to the assistive technologies as being inside the application that created the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Plug.html)

`Plug`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Socket.html)

`Socket`An AtkStateSet is a read-only representation of the full set of `AtkStates`
that apply to an object at a given time. This set is not meant to be
modified, but rather created when [ AtkObjectExt::ref_state_set()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.AtkObjectExt.html#tymethod.ref_state_set) is called.

An interface whereby an object allows its backing content to be streamed to clients. Typical implementors would be images or icons, HTML content, or multimedia display/rendering widgets.

[ Table](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Table.html) should be implemented by components which present
elements ordered via rows and columns. It may also be used to
present tree-structured information if the nodes of the trees can
be said to contain multiple “columns”. Individual elements of an

[are typically referred to as “cells”. Those cells should implement the interface](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Table.html)

`Table`[, but](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TableCell.html)

`TableCell``Atk` doesn’t require
them to be direct children of the current [. They can be grand-children, grand-grand-children etc.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Table.html)

`Table`[provides the API needed to get a individual cell based on the row and column numbers.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Table.html)

`Table`[ Text](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Text.html) should be implemented by

`AtkObjects` on behalf of widgets
that have text content which is either attributed or otherwise

cairo-rs = "0.13"

# pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/pango/index.html

## Expand description

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [Pango](https://docs.gtk.org/Pango/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

Pango **1.38** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.56.0`.

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
pango = "0.13"
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
**pango** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- `pub use ffi;`

- Traits and essential types intended for blanket imports.

- Flags that influence the behavior of`Pango::Layout::deserialize()`.
- Flags influencing the shaping process.
- These flags affect how Pango treats characters that are normally not visible in the output.

- An enumeration that affects baseline shifts between runs.
- An enumeration that affects font sizes for superscript and subscript positioning and for (emulated) Small Caps.
- An enumeration specifying the width of the font relative to other designs within a family.
- An enumeration specifying the various slant styles possible for a font.
- An enumeration that affects how Pango treats characters during shaping.
- An enumeration specifying capitalization variant of the font.
- An enumeration specifying the weight (boldness) of a font.

- Whether the segment should be shifted to center around the baseline.
- Whether this run holds ellipsized text.
- Whether to add a hyphen at the end of the run during shaping.
- A`PangoGlyph`value that indicates a zero-width empty glpyh.
- A`PangoGlyph`value for invalid input.
- Flag used in`PangoGlyph`to turn a`gunichar`value of a valid Unicode character into an unknown-character glyph for that`gunichar`.
- The scale between dimensions used for Pango distances and device units.
- The scale factor for one magnification step (1.2).
- The scale factor for normal size (1.0).
- The scale factor for one shrinking step (1 / 1.2).
- The scale factor for three magnification steps (1.2 * 1.2 * 1.2).
- The scale factor for three shrinking steps (1 / (1.2 * 1.2 * 1.2)).
- The scale factor for two magnification steps (1.2 * 1.2).
- The scale factor for two shrinking steps (1 / (1.2 * 1.2)).

- Converts extents from Pango units to device units.
- Searches a string the first character that has a strong direction, according to the Unicode bidirectional algorithm.
- Locates a paragraph boundary in @text.
- Checks if a character that should not be normally rendered.
- Breaks a piece of text into segments with consistent directional level and font.
- Like`pango_itemize()`, but with an explicitly specified base direction.
- Parses marked-up text to create a plain-text string and an attribute list.
- Parses a font stretch.
- Parses a font style.
- Parses a font variant.
- Parses a font weight.
- Quantizes the thickness and position of a line to whole device pixels.
- Convert the characters in @text into glyphs.
- Determines the inherent direction of a character.
- Converts a floating-point number to Pango units.
- Converts a number in Pango units to floating-point.
- Returns the encoded version of Pango available at run-time.
- Checks that the Pango library in use is compatible with the given version.
- Returns the version of Pango available at run-time.

# AboutDialog in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.AboutDialog.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct AboutDialog { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The GtkAboutDialog offers a simple way to display information about
a program like its logo, name, copyright, website and license. It is
also possible to give credits to the authors, documenters, translators
and artists who have worked on the program. An about dialog is typically
opened when the user selects the `About` option from the `Help` menu.
All parts of the dialog are optional.

About dialogs often contain links and email addresses. GtkAboutDialog
displays these as clickable links. By default, it calls [ show_uri_on_window()](https://gtk-rs.org/functions/fn.show_uri_on_window.html)
when a user clicks one. The behaviour can be overridden with the

`signal::AboutDialog::activate-link` signal.To specify a person with an email address, use a string like “Edgar Allan Poe <edgar`poe`>”. To specify a website with a title, use a string like “GTK+ team http://www.gtk.org”.

To make constructing a GtkAboutDialog as convenient as possible, you can
use the function `gtk_show_about_dialog()` which constructs and shows a dialog
and keeps it around so that it can be shown again.

Note that GTK+ sets a default title of `_("About `s`")` on the dialog
window (where `s` is replaced by the name of the application, but in
order to ensure proper translation of the title, applications should
set the title property explicitly when constructing a GtkAboutDialog,
as shown in the following example:

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
GdkPixbuf *example_logo = gdk_pixbuf_new_from_file ("./logo.png", NULL);
gtk_show_about_dialog (NULL,
                       "program-name", "ExampleCode",
                       "logo", example_logo,
                       "title", _("About ExampleCode"),
                       NULL);
```

The caller of the `bitflags!` macro can chose to allow or

The caller of `from_bits_unchecked()` has to ensure that
all bits correspond to a defined flag or that extra bits

#### pub const fn [intersection](https://gtk-rs.org#method.intersection)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the intersection between the flags in `self` and
`other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains only the flags which are
present in *both* `self` *and* `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `&` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitAnd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitAnd.html)), as in

`flags & other`.Returns the union of between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags which are
present in *either* `self` *or* `other`, including any which are
present in both (see [ Self::symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AccelFlags.html#method.symmetric_difference) if that
is undesirable).

This is equivalent to using the `|` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitOr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitOr.html)), as in

Returns the difference between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags present in
`self`, except for the ones present in `other`.

It is also conceptually equivalent to the “bit-clear” operation:
`flags & !other` (and this syntax is also supported).

This is equivalent to using the `-` operator (e.g.
[ ops::Sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.Sub.html)), as in

Returns the [symmetric difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_difference) between the flags
in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains the flags present which
are present in `self` or `other`, but that are not present in
both. Equivalently, it contains the flags present in *exactly
one* of the sets `self` and `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `^` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitXor](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitXor.html)), as in
