# FlowBox in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.FlowBox.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct FlowBox { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A GtkFlowBox positions child widgets in sequence according to its orientation.

For instance, with the horizontal orientation, the widgets will be arranged from left to right, starting a new row under the previous row when necessary. Reducing the width in this case will require more rows, so a larger height will be requested.

Likewise, with the vertical orientation, the widgets will be arranged from top to bottom, starting a new column to the right when necessary. Reducing the height will require more columns, so a larger width will be requested.

The size request of a GtkFlowBox alone may not be what you expect; if you
need to be able to shrink it along both axes and dynamically reflow its
children, you may have to wrap it in a [ ScrolledWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ScrolledWindow.html) to enable that.

The children of a GtkFlowBox can be dynamically sorted and filtered.

Although a GtkFlowBox must have only [ FlowBoxChild](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FlowBoxChild.html) children,
you can add any kind of widget to it via

[, and a GtkFlowBoxChild widget will automatically be inserted between the box and the widget.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.ContainerExt.html#tymethod.add)

`ContainerExt::add()`Also see [ ListBox](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListBox.html).

GtkFlowBox was added in GTK+ 3.12.

**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
flowbox
├── flowboxchild
│   ╰── <child>
├── flowboxchild
│   ╰── <child>
┊
╰── [rubberband]
```
GtkFlowBox uses a single CSS node with name flowbox. GtkFlowBoxChild uses a single CSS node with name flowboxchild. For rubberband selection, a subnode with name rubberband is used.

# FontButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.FontButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct FontButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ FontButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontButton.html) is a button which displays the currently selected
font an allows to open a font chooser dialog to change the font.
It is suitable widget for selecting a font in a preference dialog.

GtkFontButton has a single CSS node with name button and style class .font.

# FontChooserWidget in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.FontChooserWidget.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct FontChooserWidget { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ FontChooserWidget](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontChooserWidget.html) widget lists the available fonts,
styles and sizes, allowing the user to select a font. It is
used in the

[widget to provide a dialog box for selecting fonts.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontChooserDialog.html)

`FontChooserDialog`To set the font which is initially selected, use
[ FontChooserExt::set_font()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontChooserExt.html#tymethod.set_font) or

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontChooserExt.html#tymethod.set_font_desc)

`FontChooserExt::set_font_desc()`To get the selected font use [ FontChooserExt::font()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontChooserExt.html#tymethod.font) or

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontChooserExt.html#tymethod.font_desc)

`FontChooserExt::font_desc()`To change the text which is shown in the preview area, use
[ FontChooserExt::set_preview_text()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontChooserExt.html#tymethod.set_preview_text).

GtkFontChooserWidget has a single CSS node with name fontchooser.

# FontChooserLevel in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.FontChooserLevel.html

`pub struct FontChooserLevel { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`v3_24`## Expand description

This enumeration specifies the granularity of font selection that is desired in a font chooser.

This enumeration may be extended in the future; applications should ignore unknown values.

Allow selecting a font family

# GLArea in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.GLArea.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct GLArea { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ GLArea](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GLArea.html) is a widget that allows drawing with OpenGL.

[ GLArea](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GLArea.html) sets up its own

[for the window it creates, and creates a custom GL framebuffer that the widget will do GL rendering onto. It also ensures that this framebuffer is the default GL rendering target when rendering.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/gl_context/struct.GLContext.html)

`gdk::GLContext`In order to draw, you have to connect to the `signal::GLArea::render` signal,
or subclass [ GLArea](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GLArea.html) and override the

`GtkGLAreaClass.render()` virtual
function.The [ GLArea](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GLArea.html) widget ensures that the

[is associated with the widget’s drawing area, and it is kept updated when the size and position of the drawing area changes.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/gl_context/struct.GLContext.html)

`gdk::GLContext`The simplest way to draw using OpenGL commands in a [ GLArea](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GLArea.html) is to
create a widget instance and connect to the

`signal::GLArea::render` signal:**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
  // create a GtkGLArea instance
  GtkWidget *gl_area = gtk_gl_area_new ();
  // connect to the "render" signal
  g_signal_connect (gl_area, "render", G_CALLBACK (render), NULL);
```
The `render()` function will be called when the [ GLArea](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GLArea.html) is ready
for you to draw its content:

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
  static gboolean
  render (GtkGLArea *area, GdkGLContext *context)
  {
    // inside this function it's safe to use GL; the given
    // #GdkGLContext has been made current to the drawable
    // surface used by the #GtkGLArea and the viewport has
    // already been set to be the size of the allocation
    // we can start by clearing the buffer
    glClearColor (0, 0, 0, 0);
    glClear (GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
    // draw your object
    draw_an_object ();
    // we completed our drawing; the draw commands will be
    // flushed at the end of the signal emission chain, and
    // the buffers will be drawn on the window
    return TRUE;
  }
```
If you need to initialize OpenGL state, e.g. buffer objects or
shaders, you should use the `signal::Widget::realize` signal; you
can use the `signal::Widget::unrealize` signal to clean up. Since the
[ gdk::GLContext](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/gl_context/struct.GLContext.html) creation and initialization may fail, you will
need to check for errors, using

[. An example of how to safely initialize the GL state is:](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GLAreaExt.html#tymethod.error)

`GLAreaExt::error()`**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
  static void
  on_realize (GtkGLarea *area)
  {
    // We need to make the context current if we want to
    // call GL API
    gtk_gl_area_make_current (area);
    // If there were errors during the initialization or
    // when trying to make the context current, this
    // function will return a #GError for you to catch
    if (gtk_gl_area_get_error (area) != NULL)
      return;
    // You can also use gtk_gl_area_set_error() in order
    // to show eventual initialization errors on the
    // GtkGLArea widget itself
    GError *internal_error = NULL;
    init_buffer_objects (&error);
    if (error != NULL)
      {
        gtk_gl_area_set_error (area, error);
        g_error_free (error);
        return;
      }
    init_shaders (&error);
    if (error != NULL)
      {
        gtk_gl_area_set_error (area, error);
        g_error_free (error);
        return;
      }
  }
```
If you need to change the options for creating the [ gdk::GLContext](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/gl_context/struct.GLContext.html)
you should use the

`signal::GLArea::create-context` signal.[ GLAreaExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GLAreaExt.html),

# Gesture in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Gesture.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Gesture { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ Gesture](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html) is the base object for gesture recognition, although this
object is quite generalized to serve as a base for multi-touch gestures,
it is suitable to implement single-touch and pointer-based gestures (using
the special

`None`[value for these).](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/event_sequence/struct.EventSequence.html)

`gdk::EventSequence`The number of touches that a [ Gesture](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html) need to be recognized is controlled
by the

`property::Gesture::n-points` property, if a gesture is keeping track of less
or more than that number of sequences, it won’t check wether the gesture
is recognized.As soon as the gesture has the expected number of touches, the gesture will
run the `signal::Gesture::check` signal regularly on input events until the gesture
is recognized, the criteria to consider a gesture as “recognized” is left to
[ Gesture](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html) subclasses.

A recognized gesture will then emit the following signals:

- `signal::Gesture::begin`when the gesture is recognized.
- A number of `signal::Gesture::update`, whenever an input event is processed.
- `signal::Gesture::end`when the gesture is no longer recognized.

In order to receive events, a gesture needs to either set a propagation phase
through [ EventControllerExt::set_propagation_phase()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.EventControllerExt.html#tymethod.set_propagation_phase), or feed those manually
through

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.EventControllerExt.html#tymethod.handle_event)

`EventControllerExt::handle_event()`In the capture phase, events are propagated from the toplevel down to the target widget, and gestures that are attached to containers above the widget get a chance to interact with the event before it reaches the target.

After the capture phase, GTK+ emits the traditional `signal::Widget::button-press-event`,
`signal::Widget::button-release-event`, `signal::Widget::touch-event`, etc signals. Gestures
with the [ PropagationPhase::Target](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.PropagationPhase.html#variant.Target) phase are fed events from the default

`signal::Widget::event`
handlers.In the bubble phase, events are propagated up from the target widget to the toplevel, and gestures that are attached to containers above the widget get a chance to interact with events that have not been handled yet.

Whenever input interaction happens, a single event may trigger a cascade of
`GtkGestures`, both across the parents of the widget receiving the event and
in parallel within an individual widget. It is a responsibility of the
widgets using those gestures to set the state of touch sequences accordingly
in order to enable cooperation of gestures around the `GdkEventSequences`
triggering those.

Within a widget, gestures can be grouped through [ GestureExt::group_with()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureExt.html#tymethod.group_with),
grouped gestures synchronize the state of sequences, so calling

[on one will effectively propagate the state throughout the group.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureExt.html#tymethod.set_sequence_state)

`GestureExt::set_sequence_state()`By default, all sequences start out in the [ EventSequenceState::None](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.EventSequenceState.html#variant.None) state,
sequences in this state trigger the gesture event handler, but event
propagation will continue unstopped by gestures.

If a sequence enters into the [ EventSequenceState::Denied](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.EventSequenceState.html#variant.Denied) state, the gesture
group will effectively ignore the sequence, letting events go unstopped
through the gesture, but the “slot” will still remain occupied while
the touch is active.

If a sequence enters in the [ EventSequenceState::Claimed](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.EventSequenceState.html#variant.Claimed) state, the gesture
group will grab all interaction on the sequence, by:

- Setting the same sequence to `EventSequenceState::Denied`
- calling `signal::Gesture::cancel`on every gesture in widgets underneath in the propagation chain.
- Stopping event propagation after the gesture group handles the event.

Note: if a sequence is set early to [ EventSequenceState::Claimed](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.EventSequenceState.html#variant.Claimed) on

`GDK_TOUCH_BEGIN`/`GDK_BUTTON_PRESS` (so those events are captured before
reaching the event widget, this implies [), one similar event will emulated if the sequence changes to](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.PropagationPhase.html#variant.Capture)

`PropagationPhase::Capture`[. This way event coherence is preserved before event propagation is unstopped again.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.EventSequenceState.html#variant.Denied)

`EventSequenceState::Denied`Sequence states can’t be changed freely, see [ GestureExt::set_sequence_state()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureExt.html#tymethod.set_sequence_state)
to know about the possible lifetimes of a

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/event_sequence/struct.EventSequence.html)

`gdk::EventSequence`On the platforms that support it, [ Gesture](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html) will handle transparently
touchpad gesture events. The only precautions users of

[should do to enable this support are:](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html)

`Gesture`- Enabling `gdk::EventMask::TOUCHPAD_GESTURE_MASK``GdkWindows`
- If the gesture has `PropagationPhase::None``GDK_TOUCHPAD_SWIPE`and`GDK_TOUCHPAD_PINCH`are handled by the`Gesture`

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

## Expand description

If the `self` is active, this function returns `true``x` and `y` with the coordinates of the current point,
as an offset to the starting drag point.

`true`

X offset for the current point

Y offset for the current point

If the `self` is active, this function returns `true``x` and `y` with the drag start coordinates,
in window-relative coordinates.

`true`

X coordinate for the drag start point

Y coordinate for the drag start point

This signal is emitted whenever dragging starts.

X coordinate, relative to the widget allocation

Y coordinate, relative to the widget allocation

This signal is emitted whenever the dragging is finished.

X offset, relative to the start point

Y offset, relative to the start point

This signal is emitted whenever the dragging point moves.

X offset, relative to the start point

Y offset, relative to the start point

# GestureLongPress in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.GestureLongPress.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct GestureLongPress { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ GestureLongPress](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GestureLongPress.html) is a

[implementation able to recognize long presses, triggering the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html)

`Gesture``signal::GestureLongPress::pressed` after the
timeout is exceeded.If the touchpoint is lifted before the timeout passes, or if it drifts
too far of the initial press point, the `signal::GestureLongPress::cancelled`
signal will be emitted.

# GestureMultiPress in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.GestureMultiPress.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct GestureMultiPress { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ GestureMultiPress](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GestureMultiPress.html) is a

[implementation able to recognize multiple clicks on a nearby zone, which can be listened for through the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html)

`Gesture``signal::GestureMultiPress::pressed` signal. Whenever time or distance between
clicks exceed the GTK+ defaults, `signal::GestureMultiPress::stopped` is emitted,
and the click counter is reset.Callers may also restrict the area that is considered valid for a >1
touch/button press through [ set_area()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GestureMultiPress.html#method.set_area), so any
click happening outside that area is considered to be a first click of
its own.

# GesturePan in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.GesturePan.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct GesturePan { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ GesturePan](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GesturePan.html) is a

[implementation able to recognize pan gestures, those are drags that are locked to happen along one axis. The axis that a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html)

`Gesture`[handles is defined at construct time, and can be changed through](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GesturePan.html)

`GesturePan`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GesturePan.html#method.set_orientation)

`set_orientation()`When the gesture starts to be recognized, [ GesturePan](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GesturePan.html) will
attempt to determine as early as possible whether the sequence
is moving in the expected direction, and denying the sequence if
this does not happen.

Once a panning gesture along the expected axis is recognized,
the `signal::GesturePan::pan` signal will be emitted as input events
are received, containing the offset in the given axis.

# GestureSingle in gtk - Rust

[ GestureSingle](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GestureSingle.html) is a subclass of

[, optimized (although not restricted) for dealing with mouse and single-touch gestures. Under interaction, these gestures stick to the first interacting sequence, which is accessible through](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Gesture.html)

`Gesture`[while the gesture is being interacted with.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureSingleExt.html#tymethod.current_sequence)

`GestureSingleExt::current_sequence()`By default gestures react to both `GDK_BUTTON_PRIMARY` and touch
events, [ GestureSingleExt::set_touch_only()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureSingleExt.html#tymethod.set_touch_only) can be used to change the
touch behavior. Callers may also specify a different mouse button number
to interact with through

[, or react to any mouse button by setting 0. While the gesture is active, the button being currently pressed can be known through](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureSingleExt.html#tymethod.set_button)

`GestureSingleExt::set_button()`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GestureSingleExt.html#tymethod.current_button)

}## Expand description

Sets the button number `self` listens to. If non-0, every
button press from a different button number will be ignored.
Touch events implicitly match with button 1.

button number to listen to, or 0 for any button

If `touch_only` is [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),

`self` will only handle events of type
`GDK_TOUCH_BEGIN`, `GDK_TOUCH_UPDATE` or `GDK_TOUCH_END`. If [, mouse events will be handled too.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`false`whether `self` handles only touch events

[ velocity()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GestureSwipe.html#method.velocity) can be called on eg. a

# Grid in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Grid.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Grid { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkGrid is a container which arranges its child widgets in rows and columns, with arbitrary positions and horizontal/vertical spans.

Children are added using [ GridExt::attach()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GridExt.html#tymethod.attach). They can span multiple
rows or columns. It is also possible to add a child next to an
existing child, using

[. The behaviour of GtkGrid when several children occupy the same grid cell is undefined.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GridExt.html#tymethod.attach_next_to)

`GridExt::attach_next_to()`GtkGrid can be used like a [ Box](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Box.html) by just using

[, which will place children next to each other in the direction determined by the](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.ContainerExt.html#tymethod.add)

`ContainerExt::add()``property::Orientable::orientation` property. However, if all you want is a
single row or column, then [is the preferred widget.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Box.html)

`Box`GtkGrid uses a single CSS node with name grid.

# HeaderBar in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.HeaderBar.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct HeaderBar { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkHeaderBar is similar to a horizontal [ Box](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Box.html). It allows children to
be placed at the start or the end. In addition, it allows a title and
subtitle to be displayed. The title will be centered with respect to
the width of the box, even if the children at either side take up
different amounts of space. The height of the titlebar will be
set to provide sufficient space for the subtitle, even if none is
currently set. If a subtitle is not needed, the space reservation
can be turned off with

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.HeaderBarExt.html#tymethod.set_has_subtitle)

`HeaderBarExt::set_has_subtitle()`GtkHeaderBar can add typical window frame controls, such as minimize, maximize and close buttons, or the window icon.

For these reasons, GtkHeaderBar is the natural choice for use as the custom
titlebar widget of a [ Window](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Window.html) (see

[), as it gives features typical of titlebars while allowing the addition of child widgets.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkWindowExt.html#tymethod.set_titlebar)

Sets a custom title for the [ HeaderBar](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.HeaderBar.html).

The title should help a user identify the current view. This
supersedes any title set by [ set_title()](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.HeaderBarExt.html#tymethod.set_title) or

[. To achieve the same style as the builtin title and subtitle, use the “title” and “subtitle” style classes.](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.HeaderBarExt.html#tymethod.set_subtitle)

`set_subtitle()`You should set the custom title to [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), for the header title
label to be visible again.

a custom widget to use for a title

Sets the decoration layout for this header bar, overriding
the `property::Settings::gtk-decoration-layout` setting.

There can be valid reasons for overriding the setting, such as a header bar design that does not allow for buttons to take room on the right, or only offers room for a single close button. Split header bars are another example for overriding the setting.

The format of the string is button names, separated by commas. A colon separates the buttons that should appear on the left from those on the right. Recognized button names are minimize, maximize, close, icon (the window icon) and menu (a menu button for the fallback app menu).

For example, “menu:minimize,maximize,close” specifies a menu on the left, and minimize, maximize and close buttons on the right.

a decoration layout, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) to
unset the layout

Sets the subtitle of the [ HeaderBar](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.HeaderBar.html). The title should give a user
an additional detail to help him identify the current view.

Note that GtkHeaderBar by default reserves room for the subtitle,
even if none is currently set. If this is not desired, set the
`property::HeaderBar::has-subtitle` property to [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).

# IMContext in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.IMContext.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct IMContext { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ IMContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IMContext.html) defines the interface for GTK+ input methods. An input method
is used by GTK+ text input widgets like

[to map from key events to Unicode character strings.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Entry.html)

`Entry`The default input method can be set programmatically via the
`property::Settings::gtk-im-module` GtkSettings property. Alternatively, you may set
the GTK_IM_MODULE environment variable as documented in
[Running GTK+ Applications][gtk-running].

The `Entry``property::Entry::im-module` and `TextView``property::TextView::im-module`
properties may also be used to set input methods for specific widget
instances. For instance, a certain entry widget might be expected to contain
certain characters which would be easier to input with a certain input
method.

An input method may consume multiple key events in sequence and finally output the composed result. This is called preediting, and an input method may provide feedback about this process by displaying the intermediate composition states as preedit text. For instance, the default GTK+ input method implements the input of arbitrary Unicode code points by holding down the Control and Shift keys and then typing “U” followed by the hexadecimal digits of the code point. When releasing the Control and Shift keys, preediting ends and the character is inserted as text. Ctrl+Shift+u20AC for example results in the € sign.

Additional input methods can be made available for use by GTK+ widgets as
loadable modules. An input method module is a small shared library which
implements a subclass of [ IMContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IMContext.html) or

[and exports these four functions:](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IMContextSimple.html)

`IMContextSimple`**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

`void im_module_init(GTypeModule *module);`This function should register the `GType` of the [ IMContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IMContext.html) subclass which
implements the input method by means of

`g_type_module_register_type()`. Note
that `g_type_register_static()` cannot be used as the type needs to be
registered dynamically.**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

`void im_module_exit(void);`Here goes any cleanup code your input method might require on module unload.

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
void im_module_list(const GtkIMContextInfo ***contexts, int *n_contexts)
{
  *contexts = info_list;
  *n_contexts = G_N_ELEMENTS (info_list);
}
```
This function returns the list of input methods provided by the module. The
example implementation above shows a common solution and simply returns a
pointer to statically defined array of `GtkIMContextInfo` items for each
provided input method.

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

`GtkIMContext * im_module_create(const gchar *context_id);`This function should return a pointer to a newly created instance of the
[ IMContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IMContext.html) subclass identified by

`context_id`. The context ID is the same
as specified in the `GtkIMContextInfo` array returned by `im_module_list()`.After a new loadable input method module has been installed on the system,
the configuration file `gtk.immodules` needs to be
regenerated by [gtk-query-immodules-3.0][gtk-query-immodules-3.0],
in order for the new input method to become available to GTK+ applications.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

# IMContextSimple in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.IMContextSimple.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct IMContextSimple { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkIMContextSimple is a simple input method context supporting table-based input methods. It has a built-in table of compose sequences that is derived from the X11 Compose files.

GtkIMContextSimple reads additional compose sequences from the first of the following files that is found: ~/.config/gtk-3.0/Compose, ~/.XCompose, /usr/share/X11/locale/$locale/Compose (for locales that have a nontrivial Compose file). The syntax of these files is described in the Compose(5) manual page.

GtkIMContextSimple also supports numeric entry of Unicode characters by typing Ctrl-Shift-u, followed by a hexadecimal Unicode codepoint. For example, Ctrl-Shift-u 1 2 3 Enter yields U+0123 LATIN SMALL LETTER G WITH CEDILLA, i.e. ģ.

Gets the base scale for the icon. The base scale is a scale for the icon that was specified by the icon theme creator. For instance an icon drawn for a high-dpi screen with window scale 2 for a base size of 32 will be 64 pixels tall and have a base scale of 2.

This may be different than the actual size of image; an example of this is small emblem icons that can be attached to a larger icon. These icons will be given the same base size as the larger icons to which they are attached.

Note that for scaled icons the base size does not include the base scale.

Loads an icon, modifying it to match the system colours for the foreground,
success, warning and error colors provided. If the icon is not a symbolic
one, the function will return the result from [ load_icon()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconInfo.html#method.load_icon).

This allows loading symbolic icons that will match the system theme.

Unless you are implementing a widget, you will want to use
`g_themed_icon_new_with_default_fallbacks()` to load the icon.

As implementation details, the icon loaded needs to be of SVG type, contain the “symbolic” term as the last component of the icon name, and use the “fg”, “success”, “warning” and “error” CSS styles in the SVG file itself.

See the [Symbolic Icons Specification](http://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/SymbolicIcons)
for more information about symbolic icons.

Convert from underlying bit representation, preserving all bits (even those not corresponding to a defined flag).

The caller of the `bitflags!` macro can chose to allow or
disallow extra bits for their bitflags type.

The caller of `from_bits_unchecked()` has to ensure that
all bits correspond to a defined flag or that extra bits
are valid for this bitflags type.

#### pub const fn [intersection](https://gtk-rs.org#method.intersection)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the intersection between the flags in `self` and
`other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains only the flags which are
present in *both* `self` *and* `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `&` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitAnd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitAnd.html)), as in

`flags & other`.Returns the union of between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags which are
present in *either* `self` *or* `other`, including any which are
present in both (see [ Self::symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconLookupFlags.html#method.symmetric_difference) if that
is undesirable).

This is equivalent to using the `|` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitOr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitOr.html)), as in

#### pub const fn [difference](https://gtk-rs.org#method.difference)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the difference between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags present in
`self`, except for the ones present in `other`.

It is also conceptually equivalent to the “bit-clear” operation:
`flags & !other` (and this syntax is also supported).

This is equivalent to using the `-` operator (e.g.
[ ops::Sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.Sub.html)), as in

`flags - other`.[source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gtk/auto/flags.rs.html#763-809)#### pub const fn [symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org#method.symmetric_difference)(self, other: Self) -> Self

#### pub const fn [symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org#method.symmetric_difference)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the [symmetric difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_difference) between the flags
in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains the flags present which
are present in `self` or `other`, but that are not present in
both. Equivalently, it contains the flags present in *exactly
one* of the sets `self` and `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `^` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitXor](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitXor.html)), as in

}Adds a resource path that will be looked at when looking for icons, similar to search paths.

This function should be used to make application-specific icons available as part of the icon theme.

The resources are considered as part of the hicolor icon theme
and must be located in subdirectories that are defined in the
hicolor icon theme, such as ``path`/16x16/actions/run.png`.
Icons that are directly placed in the resource path instead
of a subdirectory are also considered as ultimate fallback.

# IconTheme in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.IconTheme.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct IconTheme { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ IconTheme](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconTheme.html) provides a facility for looking up icons by name
and size. The main reason for using a name rather than simply
providing a filename is to allow different icons to be used
depending on what “icon theme” is selected
by the user. The operation of icon themes on Linux and Unix
follows the

[Icon Theme Specification](http://www.freedesktop.org/Standards/icon-theme-spec)There is a fallback icon theme, named

`hicolor`, where applications
should install their icons, but additional icon themes can be installed
as operating system vendors and users choose.Named icons are similar to the deprecated [Stock Items][gtkstock], and the distinction between the two may be a bit confusing. A few things to keep in mind:

-
Stock images usually are used in conjunction with [Stock Items][gtkstock], such as `GTK_STOCK_OK`or`GTK_STOCK_OPEN`. Named icons are easier to set up and therefore are more useful for new icons that an application wants to add, such as application icons or window icons.
-
Stock images can only be loaded at the symbolic sizes defined by the `IconSize``gtk_icon_size_register()`, while named icons are more flexible and any pixel size can be specified.
-
Because stock images are closely tied to stock items, and thus to actions in the user interface, stock images may come in multiple variants for different widget states or writing directions.

A good rule of thumb is that if there is a stock image for what
you want to use, use it, otherwise use a named icon. It turns
out that internally stock images are generally defined in
terms of one or more named icons. (An example of the
more than one case is icons that depend on writing direction;
`GTK_STOCK_GO_FORWARD` uses the two themed icons
“gtk-stock-go-forward-ltr” and “gtk-stock-go-forward-rtl”.)

In many cases, named themes are used indirectly, via [ Image](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Image.html)
or stock items, rather than directly, but looking up icons
directly is also simple. The

[object acts as a database of all the icons in the current theme. You can create new](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconTheme.html)

`IconTheme`[objects, but it’s much more efficient to use the standard icon theme for the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconTheme.html)

`IconTheme`[so that the icon information is shared with other people looking up icons.](https://gtk-rs.org/gdk/auto/screen/struct.Screen.html)

`gdk::Screen`**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
GError *error = NULL;
GtkIconTheme *icon_theme;
GdkPixbuf *pixbuf;
icon_theme = gtk_icon_theme_get_default ();
pixbuf = gtk_icon_theme_load_icon (icon_theme,
                                   "my-icon-name", // icon name
                                   48, // icon size
                                   0,  // flags
                                   &error);
if (!pixbuf)
  {
    g_warning ("Couldn’t load icon: %s", error->message);
    g_error_free (error);
  }
else
  {
    // Use the pixbuf
    g_object_unref (pixbuf);
  }
```

# IconView in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.IconView.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct IconView { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ IconView](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconView.html) provides an alternative view on a

[. It displays the model as a grid of icons with labels. Like](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeModel.html)

`TreeModel`[, it allows to select one or multiple items (depending on the selection mode, see](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeView.html)

`TreeView`[). In addition to selection with the arrow keys,](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.IconViewExt.html#tymethod.set_selection_mode)

`IconViewExt::set_selection_mode()`[supports rubberband selection, which is controlled by dragging the pointer.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconView.html)

`IconView`Note that if the tree model is backed by an actual tree store (as
opposed to a flat list where the mapping to icons is obvious),
[ IconView](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.IconView.html) will only display the first level of the tree and
ignore the tree’s branches.

**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
iconview.view
╰── [rubberband]
```
GtkIconView has a single CSS node with name iconview and style class .view. For rubberband selection, a subnode with name rubberband is used.

Moves the alignments of `self` to the position specified by `path`.
`row_align` determines where the row is placed, and `col_align` determines
where `column` is placed. Both are expected to be between 0.0 and 1.0.
0.0 means left/top alignment, 1.0 means right/bottom alignment, 0.5 means
center.

If `use_align` is [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), then the alignment arguments are ignored, and the
tree does the minimum amount of work to scroll the item onto the screen.
This means that the item will be scrolled to the edge closest to its current
position. If the item is currently visible on the screen, nothing is done.

This function only works if the model is set, and `path` is a valid row on
the model. If the model changes before the `self` is realized, the
centered path will be modified to reflect this change.

The path of the item to move to.

# InfoBar in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.InfoBar.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct InfoBar { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ InfoBar](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InfoBar.html) is a widget that can be used to show messages to
the user without showing a dialog. It is often temporarily shown
at the top or bottom of a document. In contrast to

[, which has a action area at the bottom,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Dialog.html)

`Dialog`[has an action area at the side.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InfoBar.html)

`InfoBar`The API of [ InfoBar](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InfoBar.html) is very similar to

[, allowing you to add buttons to the action area with](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Dialog.html)

`Dialog`[or](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.InfoBarExt.html#tymethod.add_button)

`InfoBarExt::add_button()``gtk_info_bar_new_with_buttons()`. The sensitivity of action widgets
can be controlled with [. To add widgets to the main content area of a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.InfoBarExt.html#tymethod.set_response_sensitive)

`InfoBarExt::set_response_sensitive()`[, use](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InfoBar.html)

`InfoBar`[and add your widgets to the container.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.InfoBarExt.html#tymethod.content_area)

`InfoBarExt::content_area()`Similar to [ MessageDialog](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MessageDialog.html), the contents of a

[can by classified as error message, warning, informational message, etc, by using](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InfoBar.html)

`InfoBar`[. GTK+ may use the message type to determine how the message is displayed.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.InfoBarExt.html#tymethod.set_message_type)

`InfoBarExt::set_message_type()`A simple example for using a [ InfoBar](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InfoBar.html):

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
GtkWidget *widget, *message_label, *content_area;
GtkWidget *grid;
GtkInfoBar *bar;
// set up info bar
widget = gtk_info_bar_new ();
bar = GTK_INFO_BAR (widget);
grid = gtk_grid_new ();
gtk_widget_set_no_show_all (widget, TRUE);
message_label = gtk_label_new ("");
content_area = gtk_info_bar_get_content_area (bar);
gtk_container_add (GTK_CONTAINER (content_area),
                   message_label);
gtk_info_bar_add_button (bar,
                         _("_OK"),
                         GTK_RESPONSE_OK);
g_signal_connect (bar,
                  "response",
                  G_CALLBACK (gtk_widget_hide),
                  NULL);
gtk_grid_attach (GTK_GRID (grid),
                 widget,
                 0, 2, 1, 1);
// ...
// show an error message
gtk_label_set_text (GTK_LABEL (message_label), "An error occurred!");
gtk_info_bar_set_message_type (bar,
                               GTK_MESSAGE_ERROR);
gtk_widget_show (bar);
```
The GtkInfoBar implementation of the GtkBuildable interface exposes the content area and action area as internal children with the names “content_area” and “action_area”.

GtkInfoBar supports a custom `<action-widgets>` element, which can contain
multiple `<action-widget>` elements. The “response” attribute specifies a
numeric response, and the content of the element is the id of widget
(which should be a child of the dialogs `action_area`).

GtkInfoBar has a single CSS node with name infobar. The node may get one of the style classes .info, .warning, .error or .question, depending on the message type.

# InputHints in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.InputHints.html

`pub struct InputHints { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Describes hints that might be taken into account by input methods
or applications. Note that input methods may already tailor their
behaviour according to the [ InputPurpose](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.InputPurpose.html) of the entry.

Some common sense is expected when using these flags - mixing
[ LOWERCASE](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InputHints.html#associatedconstant.LOWERCASE) with any of the uppercase hints makes no sense.

This enumeration may be extended in the future; input methods should ignore unknown values.

The caller of the `bitflags!` macro can chose to allow or
disallow extra bits for their bitflags type.

The caller of `from_bits_unchecked()` has to ensure that
all bits correspond to a defined flag or that extra bits
are valid for this bitflags type.

#### pub const fn [intersection](https://gtk-rs.org#method.intersection)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the intersection between the flags in `self` and
`other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains only the flags which are
present in *both* `self` *and* `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `&` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitAnd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitAnd.html)), as in

`flags & other`.Returns the union of between the flags in `self` and `other`.

present in *either* `self` *or* `other`, including any which are
present in both (see [ Self::symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.InputHints.html#method.symmetric_difference) if that
is undesirable).

Returns the difference between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags present in
`self`, except for the ones present in `other`.

It is also conceptually equivalent to the “bit-clear” operation:
`flags & !other` (and this syntax is also supported).

This is equivalent to using the `-` operator (e.g.

#### pub const fn [symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org#method.symmetric_difference)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the [symmetric difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_difference) between the flags
in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains the flags present which
are present in `self` or `other`, but that are not present in
both. Equivalently, it contains the flags present in *exactly
one* of the sets `self` and `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `^` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitXor](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitXor.html)), as in

# InputPurpose in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/enum.InputPurpose.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum InputPurpose {
    FreeForm,
    Alpha,
    Digits,
    Number,
    Phone,
    Url,
    Email,
    Name,
    Password,
    Pin,
    Terminal,
    // some variants omitted
}
```
## Expand description

Describes primary purpose of the input widget. This information is useful for on-screen keyboards and similar input methods to decide which keys should be presented to the user.

Note that the purpose is not meant to impose a totally strict rule about allowed characters, and does not replace input validation. It is fine for an on-screen keyboard to let the user override the character set restriction that is expressed by the purpose. The application is expected to validate the entry contents, even if it specified a purpose.

The difference between [ Digits](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.InputPurpose.html#variant.Digits) and

[is that the former accepts only digits while the latter also some punctuation (like commas or points, plus, minus) and “e” or “E” as in 3.14E+000.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.InputPurpose.html#variant.Number)

`Number`This enumeration may be extended in the future; input methods should interpret unknown values as “free form”.

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Allow any character

Allow only alphabetic characters

Allow only digits

Edited field expects numbers

Edited field expects phone number

Edited field expects URL

Edited field expects email address

Edited field expects the name of a person

Allow any character, in addition to control codes

The [ Invisible](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Invisible.html) widget is used internally in GTK+, and is probably not

The caller of the `bitflags!` macro can chose to allow or
disallow extra bits for their bitflags type.

The caller of `from_bits_unchecked()` has to ensure that
all bits correspond to a defined flag or that extra bits
are valid for this bitflags type.

#### pub const fn [intersection](https://gtk-rs.org#method.intersection)(self, other: Self) -> Self

Returns the intersection between the flags in `self` and
`other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains only the flags which are
present in *both* `self` *and* `other`.

This is equivalent to using the `&` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitAnd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitAnd.html)), as in

`flags & other`.Returns the union of between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags which are
present in *either* `self` *or* `other`, including any which are
present in both (see [ Self::symmetric_difference](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.JunctionSides.html#method.symmetric_difference) if that
is undesirable).

This is equivalent to using the `|` operator (e.g.
[ ops::BitOr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/trait.BitOr.html)), as in

Returns the difference between the flags in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains all flags present in
`self`, except for the ones present in `other`.

It is also conceptually equivalent to the “bit-clear” operation:

This is equivalent to using the `-` operator (e.g.

Returns the [symmetric difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_difference) between the flags
in `self` and `other`.

Specifically, the returned set contains the flags present which
are present in `self` or `other`, but that are not present in
both. Equivalently, it contains the flags present in *exactly

# Scrollable in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Scrollable.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Scrollable { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ Scrollable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Scrollable.html) is an interface that is implemented by widgets with native
scrolling ability.

To implement this interface you should override the
`property::Scrollable::hadjustment` and `property::Scrollable::vadjustment` properties.

All scrollable widgets should do the following.

-
When a parent widget sets the scrollable child widget’s adjustments, the widget should populate the adjustments’ `property::Adjustment::lower`,`property::Adjustment::upper`,`property::Adjustment::step-increment`,`property::Adjustment::page-increment`and`property::Adjustment::page-size`properties and connect to the`signal::Adjustment::value-changed`signal.
-
Because its preferred size is the size for a fully expanded widget, the scrollable widget must be able to cope with underallocations. This means that it must accept any value passed to its `GtkWidgetClass.size_allocate()`function.
-
When the parent allocates space to the scrollable child widget, the widget should update the adjustments’ properties with new values.
-
When any of the adjustments emits the `signal::Adjustment::value-changed`signal, the scrollable widget should scroll its contents.

# LevelBar in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.LevelBar.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct LevelBar { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ LevelBar](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LevelBar.html) is a bar widget that can be used
as a level indicator. Typical use cases are displaying the strength
of a password, or showing the charge level of a battery.

Use [ LevelBarExt::set_value()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.LevelBarExt.html#tymethod.set_value) to set the current value, and

[to set the value offsets at which the bar will be considered in a different state. GTK will add a few offsets by default on the level bar:](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.LevelBarExt.html#tymethod.add_offset_value)

`LevelBarExt::add_offset_value()`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/static.LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_LOW.html)

`LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_LOW`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/static.LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_HIGH.html)

`LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_HIGH`[, with values 0.25, 0.75 and 1.0 respectively.](https://gtk-rs.org/static.LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_FULL.html)

`LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_FULL`Note that it is your responsibility to update preexisting offsets when changing the minimum or maximum value. GTK+ will simply clamp them to the new range.

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
static GtkWidget *
create_level_bar (void)
{
  GtkWidget *widget;
  GtkLevelBar *bar;
  widget = gtk_level_bar_new ();
  bar = GTK_LEVEL_BAR (widget);
  // This changes the value of the default low offset
  gtk_level_bar_add_offset_value (bar,
                                  GTK_LEVEL_BAR_OFFSET_LOW,
                                  0.10);
  // This adds a new offset to the bar; the application will
  // be able to change its color CSS like this:
  //
  // levelbar block.my-offset {
  //   background-color: magenta;
  //   border-style: solid;
  //   border-color: black;
  //   border-style: 1px;
  // }
  gtk_level_bar_add_offset_value (bar, "my-offset", 0.60);
  return widget;
}
```
The default interval of values is between zero and one, but it’s possible to
modify the interval using [ LevelBarExt::set_min_value()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.LevelBarExt.html#tymethod.set_min_value) and

[. The value will be always drawn in proportion to the admissible interval, i.e. a value of 15 with a specified interval between 10 and 20 is equivalent to a value of 0.5 with an interval between 0 and 1. When](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.LevelBarExt.html#tymethod.set_max_value)

`LevelBarExt::set_max_value()`[is used, the bar level is rendered as a finite number of separated blocks instead of a single one. The number of blocks that will be rendered is equal to the number of units specified by the admissible interval.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LevelBarMode.html#variant.Discrete)

`LevelBarMode::Discrete`For instance, to build a bar rendered with five blocks, it’s sufficient to set the minimum value to 0 and the maximum value to 5 after changing the indicator mode to discrete.

GtkLevelBar was introduced in GTK+ 3.6.

The GtkLevelBar implementation of the GtkBuildable interface supports a
custom `<offsets>` element, which can contain any number of `<offset>` elements,
each of which must have “name” and “value” attributes.

**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
levelbar[.discrete]
╰── trough
    ├── block.filled.level-name
    ┊
    ├── block.empty
    ┊
```
GtkLevelBar has a main CSS node with name levelbar and one of the style classes .discrete or .continuous and a subnode with name trough. Below the trough node are a number of nodes with name block and style class .filled or .empty. In continuous mode, there is exactly one node of each, in discrete mode, the number of filled and unfilled nodes corresponds to blocks that are drawn. The block.filled nodes also get a style class .level-name corresponding to the level for the current value.

In horizontal orientation, the nodes are always arranged from left to right, regardless of text direction.

# LinkButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.LinkButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct LinkButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A GtkLinkButton is a [ Button](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Button.html) with a hyperlink, similar to the one
used by web browsers, which triggers an action when clicked. It is useful
to show quick links to resources.

A link button is created by calling either [ new()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LinkButton.html#method.new) or

[. If using the former, the URI you pass to the constructor is used as a label for the widget.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LinkButton.html#method.with_label)

`with_label()`The URI bound to a GtkLinkButton can be set specifically using
[ LinkButtonExt::set_uri()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.LinkButtonExt.html#tymethod.set_uri), and retrieved using

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.LinkButtonExt.html#tymethod.uri)

`LinkButtonExt::uri()`By default, GtkLinkButton calls [ show_uri_on_window()](https://gtk-rs.org/functions/fn.show_uri_on_window.html) when the button is
clicked. This behaviour can be overridden by connecting to the

`signal::LinkButton::activate-link` signal and returning [from the signal handler.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`GtkLinkButton has a single CSS node with name button. To differentiate
it from a plain [ Button](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Button.html), it gets the .link style class.

# ListBox in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.ListBox.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct ListBox { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A GtkListBox is a vertical container that contains GtkListBoxRow children. These rows can be dynamically sorted and filtered, and headers can be added dynamically depending on the row content. It also allows keyboard and mouse navigation and selection like a typical list.

Using GtkListBox is often an alternative to [ TreeView](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeView.html), especially
when the list contents has a more complicated layout than what is allowed
by a

[, or when the contents is interactive (i.e. has a button in it).](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.CellRenderer.html)

`CellRenderer`Although a [ ListBox](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListBox.html) must have only

[children you can add any kind of widget to it via](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListBoxRow.html)

`ListBoxRow`[, and a](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.ContainerExt.html#tymethod.add)

`ContainerExt::add()`[widget will automatically be inserted between the list and the widget.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListBoxRow.html)

`ListBoxRow``GtkListBoxRows` can be marked as activatable or selectable. If a row
is activatable, `signal::ListBox::row-activated` will be emitted for it when
the user tries to activate it. If it is selectable, the row will be marked
as selected when the user tries to select it.

The GtkListBox widget was added in GTK+ 3.10.

The GtkListBox implementation of the [ Buildable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Buildable.html) interface supports
setting a child as the placeholder by specifying “placeholder” as the “type”
attribute of a

`<child>` element. See [for info.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.ListBoxExt.html#tymethod.set_placeholder)

`ListBoxExt::set_placeholder()`**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
list
╰── row[.activatable]
```
GtkListBox uses a single CSS node named list. Each GtkListBoxRow uses a single CSS node named row. The row nodes get the .activatable style class added when appropriate.

# ListStore in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.ListStore.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct ListStore { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ ListStore](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html) object is a list model for use with a

[widget. It implements the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeView.html)

`TreeView`[interface, and consequentialy, can use all of the methods available there. It also implements the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeModel.html)

`TreeModel`[interface so it can be sorted by the view. Finally, it also implements the tree [drag and drop][gtk3-GtkTreeView-drag-and-drop] interfaces.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeSortable.html)

`TreeSortable`The [ ListStore](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html) can accept most GObject types as a column type, though
it can’t accept all custom types. Internally, it will keep a copy of
data passed in (such as a string or a boxed pointer). Columns that
accept

`GObjects` are handled a little differently. The
[will keep a reference to the object instead of copying the value. As a result, if the object is modified, it is up to the application writer to call](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html)

`ListStore`[to emit the](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.TreeModelExt.html#tymethod.row_changed)

`TreeModelExt::row_changed()``signal::TreeModel::row_changed` signal. This most commonly affects lists with
`GdkPixbufs` stored.An example for creating a simple list store:

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
enum {
  COLUMN_STRING,
  COLUMN_INT,
  COLUMN_BOOLEAN,
  N_COLUMNS
};
{
  GtkListStore *list_store;
  GtkTreePath *path;
  GtkTreeIter iter;
  gint i;
  list_store = gtk_list_store_new (N_COLUMNS,
                                   G_TYPE_STRING,
                                   G_TYPE_INT,
                                   G_TYPE_BOOLEAN);
  for (i = 0; i < 10; i++)
    {
      gchar *some_data;
      some_data = get_some_data (i);
      // Add a new row to the model
      gtk_list_store_append (list_store, &iter);
      gtk_list_store_set (list_store, &iter,
                          COLUMN_STRING, some_data,
                          COLUMN_INT, i,
                          COLUMN_BOOLEAN,  FALSE,
                          -1);
      // As the store will keep a copy of the string internally,
      // we free some_data.
      g_free (some_data);
    }
  // Modify a particular row
  path = gtk_tree_path_new_from_string ("4");
  gtk_tree_model_get_iter (GTK_TREE_MODEL (list_store),
                           &iter,
                           path);
  gtk_tree_path_free (path);
  gtk_list_store_set (list_store, &iter,
                      COLUMN_BOOLEAN, TRUE,
                      -1);
}
```
Internally, the [ ListStore](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html) was implemented with a linked list with
a tail pointer prior to GTK+ 2.6. As a result, it was fast at data
insertion and deletion, and not fast at random data access. The

[sets the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html)

`ListStore`[flag, which means that](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeModelFlags.html#associatedconstant.ITERS_PERSIST)

`TreeModelFlags::ITERS_PERSIST``GtkTreeIters` can be cached while the row exists. Thus, if
access to a particular row is needed often and your code is expected to
run on older versions of GTK+, it is worth keeping the iter around.It is important to note that only the methods
`gtk_list_store_insert_with_values()` and `gtk_list_store_insert_with_valuesv()`
are atomic, in the sense that the row is being appended to the store and the
values filled in in a single operation with regard to [ TreeModel](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeModel.html) signaling.
In contrast, using e.g.

[and then](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkListStoreExt.html#tymethod.append)

`GtkListStoreExt::append()`[will first create a row, which triggers the](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.GtkListStoreExtManual.html#tymethod.set)

`GtkListStoreExtManual::set()``signal::TreeModel::row-inserted` signal
on [. The row, however, is still empty, and any signal handler connecting to](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html)

`ListStore``signal::TreeModel::row-inserted` on this particular store should be prepared
for the situation that the row might be empty. This is especially important
if you are wrapping the [inside a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html)

`ListStore`[and are using a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TreeModelFilter.html)

`TreeModelFilter``GtkTreeModelFilterVisibleFunc`. Using any of the non-atomic operations
to append rows to the [will cause the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ListStore.html)

`ListStore``GtkTreeModelFilterVisibleFunc` to be visited with an empty row first; the
function must be prepared for that.The GtkListStore implementation of the GtkBuildable interface allows
to specify the model columns with a `<columns>` element that may contain
multiple `<column>` elements, each specifying one model column. The “type”
attribute specifies the data type for the column.

Additionally, it is possible to specify content for the list store
in the UI definition, with the `<data>` element. It can contain multiple
`<row>` elements, each specifying to content for one row of the list model.
Inside a `<row>`, the `<col>` elements specify the content for individual cells.

Note that it is probably more common to define your models in the code, and one might consider it a layering violation to specify the content of a list store in a UI definition, data, not presentation, and common wisdom is to separate the two, as far as possible.

An example of a UI Definition fragment for a list store:

**⚠️ The following code is in xml ⚠️**

```
<object class="GtkListStore">
  <columns>
    <column type="gchararray"/>
    <column type="gchararray"/>
    <column type="gint"/>
  </columns>
  <data>
    <row>
      <col id="0">John</col>
      <col id="1">Doe</col>
      <col id="2">25</col>
    </row>
    <row>
      <col id="0">Johan</col>
      <col id="1">Dahlin</col>
      <col id="2">50</col>
    </row>
  </data>
</object>
```

# LockButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.LockButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct LockButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkLockButton is a widget that can be used in control panels or
preference dialogs to allow users to obtain and revoke authorizations
needed to operate the controls. The required authorization is represented
by a [ gio::Permission](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/permission/struct.Permission.html) object. Concrete implementations of

[may use PolicyKit or some other authorization framework. To obtain a PolicyKit-based](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/permission/struct.Permission.html)

`gio::Permission`[, use](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/permission/struct.Permission.html)

`gio::Permission``polkit_permission_new()`.If the user is not currently allowed to perform the action, but can obtain the permission, the widget looks like this:

and the user can click the button to request the permission. Depending on the platform, this may pop up an authentication dialog or ask the user to authenticate in some other way. Once the user has obtained the permission, the widget changes to this:

and the permission can be dropped again by clicking the button. If the user is not able to obtain the permission at all, the widget looks like this:

If the user has the permission and cannot drop it, the button is hidden.

The text (and tooltips) that are shown in the various cases can be adjusted
with the `property::LockButton::text-lock`, `property::LockButton::text-unlock`,
`property::LockButton::tooltip-lock`, `property::LockButton::tooltip-unlock` and
`property::LockButton::tooltip-not-authorized` properties.

# Menu in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Menu.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Menu { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html) is a

[that implements a drop down menu consisting of a list of](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuShell.html)

`MenuShell`[objects which can be navigated and activated by the user to perform application functions.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuItem.html)

`MenuItem`A [ Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html) is most commonly dropped down by activating a

[in a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuItem.html)

`MenuItem`[or popped up by activating a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuBar.html)

`MenuBar`[in another](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuItem.html)

`MenuItem`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html)

`Menu`A [ Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html) can also be popped up by activating a

[. Other composite widgets such as the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ComboBox.html)

`ComboBox`[can pop up a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Notebook.html)

`Notebook`[as well.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html)

`Menu`Applications can display a [ Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html) as a popup menu by calling the

`gtk_menu_popup()` function. The example below shows how an application
can pop up a menu when the 3rd mouse button is pressed.**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
  // connect our handler which will popup the menu
  g_signal_connect_swapped (window, "button_press_event",
G_CALLBACK (my_popup_handler), menu);
```
**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
static gint
my_popup_handler (GtkWidget *widget, GdkEvent *event)
{
  GtkMenu *menu;
  GdkEventButton *event_button;
  g_return_val_if_fail (widget != NULL, FALSE);
  g_return_val_if_fail (GTK_IS_MENU (widget), FALSE);
  g_return_val_if_fail (event != NULL, FALSE);
  // The "widget" is the menu that was supplied when
  // g_signal_connect_swapped() was called.
  menu = GTK_MENU (widget);
  if (event->type == GDK_BUTTON_PRESS)
    {
      event_button = (GdkEventButton *) event;
      if (event_button->button == GDK_BUTTON_SECONDARY)
        {
          gtk_menu_popup (menu, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL,
                          event_button->button, event_button->time);
          return TRUE;
        }
    }
  return FALSE;
}
```
**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
menu
├── arrow.top
├── <child>
┊
├── <child>
╰── arrow.bottom
```
The main CSS node of GtkMenu has name menu, and there are two subnodes with name arrow, for scrolling menu arrows. These subnodes get the .top and .bottom style classes.

[source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gtk/auto/menu.rs.html#153-161)#### pub fn [from_model](https://gtk-rs.org#method.from_model)(model: &impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[MenuModel](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/menu_model/struct.MenuModel.html)>) -> [Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html)

[source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/gtk/auto/menu.rs.html#153-161)

#### pub fn [from_model](https://gtk-rs.org#method.from_model)(model: &impl [IsA](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/glib/object/trait.IsA.html)<[MenuModel](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/menu_model/struct.MenuModel.html)>) -> [Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html)

Creates a [ Menu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html) and populates it with menu items and
submenus according to

`model`.The created menu items are connected to actions found in the
[ ApplicationWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ApplicationWindow.html) to which the menu belongs - typically
by means of being attached to a widget (see

`gtk_menu_attach_to_widget()`)

# MenuShell in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.MenuShell.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct MenuShell { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ MenuShell](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuShell.html) is the abstract base class used to derive the

[and](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html)

`Menu`[subclasses.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuBar.html)

`MenuBar`A [ MenuShell](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuShell.html) is a container of

[objects arranged in a list which can be navigated, selected, and activated by the user to perform application functions. A](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuItem.html)

`MenuItem`[can have a submenu associated with it, allowing for nested hierarchical menus.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuItem.html)

`MenuItem`A menu item can be “selected”, this means that it is displayed in the prelight state, and if it has a submenu, that submenu will be popped up.

A menu is “active” when it is visible onscreen and the user is selecting from it. A menubar is not active until the user clicks on one of its menuitems. When a menu is active, passing the mouse over a submenu will pop it up.

There is also is a concept of the current menu and a current menu item. The current menu item is the selected menu item that is furthest down in the hierarchy. (Every active menu shell does not necessarily contain a selected menu item, but if it does, then the parent menu shell must also contain a selected menu item.) The current menu is the menu that contains the current menu item. It will always have a GTK grab and receive all key presses.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

# MenuButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.MenuButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct MenuButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ MenuButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuButton.html) widget is used to display a popup when clicked on.
This popup can be provided either as a

[, a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Menu.html)

`Menu`[or an abstract](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Popover.html)

`Popover`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/menu_model/struct.MenuModel.html)

`gio::MenuModel`The [ MenuButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuButton.html) widget can hold any valid child widget. That is, it
can hold almost any other standard

[. The most commonly used child is](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Widget.html)

`Widget`[. If no widget is explicitely added to the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Image.html)

`Image`[, a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuButton.html)

`MenuButton`[is automatically created, using an arrow image oriented according to](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Image.html)

`Image``property::MenuButton::direction` or the generic “open-menu-symbolic”
icon if the direction is not set.The positioning of the popup is determined by the `property::MenuButton::direction`
property of the menu button.

For menus, the `property::Widget::halign` and `property::Widget::valign` properties of the
menu are also taken into account. For example, when the direction is
[ ArrowType::Down](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.ArrowType.html#variant.Down) and the horizontal alignment is

[, the menu will be positioned below the button, with the starting edge (depending on the text direction) of the menu aligned with the starting edge of the button. If there is not enough space below the button, the menu is popped up above the button instead. If the alignment would move part of the menu offscreen, it is “pushed in”.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Align.html#variant.Start)

`Align::Start`- halign = start

- halign = center

- halign = end

- halign = start

- halign = center

- halign = end

- valign = start

- valign = center

- valign = end

- valign = center

- valign = end

# Popover in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Popover.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Popover { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkPopover is a bubble-like context window, primarily meant to
provide context-dependent information or options. Popovers are
attached to a widget, passed at construction time on [ new()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Popover.html#method.new),
or updated afterwards through

[, by default they will point to the whole widget area, although this behavior can be changed through](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PopoverExt.html#tymethod.set_relative_to)

`PopoverExt::set_relative_to()`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PopoverExt.html#tymethod.set_pointing_to)

`PopoverExt::set_pointing_to()`The position of a popover relative to the widget it is attached to
can also be changed through [ PopoverExt::set_position()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PopoverExt.html#tymethod.set_position).

By default, [ Popover](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Popover.html) performs a GTK+ grab, in order to ensure
input events get redirected to it while it is shown, and also so
the popover is dismissed in the expected situations (clicks outside
the popover, or the Esc key being pressed). If no such modal behavior
is desired on a popover,

[may be called on it to tweak its behavior.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PopoverExt.html#tymethod.set_modal)

`PopoverExt::set_modal()`GtkPopover is often used to replace menus. To facilitate this, it
supports being populated from a [ gio::MenuModel](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gio/auto/menu_model/struct.MenuModel.html), using

[. In addition to all the regular menu model features, this function supports rendering sections in the model in a more compact form, as a row of icon buttons instead of menu items.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Popover.html#method.from_model)

`from_model()`To use this rendering, set the ”display-hint” attribute of the section to ”horizontal-buttons” and set the icons of your items with the ”verb-icon” attribute.

```
<section>
  <attribute name="display-hint">horizontal-buttons</attribute>
  <item>
    <attribute name="label">Cut</attribute>
    <attribute name="action">app.cut</attribute>
    <attribute name="verb-icon">edit-cut-symbolic</attribute>
  </item>
  <item>
    <attribute name="label">Copy</attribute>
    <attribute name="action">app.copy</attribute>
    <attribute name="verb-icon">edit-copy-symbolic</attribute>
  </item>
  <item>
    <attribute name="label">Paste</attribute>
    <attribute name="action">app.paste</attribute>
    <attribute name="verb-icon">edit-paste-symbolic</attribute>
  </item>
</section>
```
GtkPopover has a single css node called popover. It always gets the
.background style class and it gets the .menu style class if it is
menu-like (e.g. [ PopoverMenu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PopoverMenu.html) or created using

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Popover.html#method.from_model)

`from_model()`Particular uses of GtkPopover, such as touch selection popups
or magnifiers in [ Entry](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Entry.html) or

[get style classes like .touch-selection or .magnifier to differentiate from plain popovers.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.TextView.html)

`TextView`[ PopoverExt](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.PopoverExt.html),

`model`. The popover is pointed to the `relative_to` widget.The created buttons are connected to actions found in the
[ ApplicationWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ApplicationWindow.html) to which the popover belongs - typically
by means of being attached to a widget that is contained within
the

`GtkApplicationWindows` widget hierarchy.Actions can also be added using [ WidgetExt::insert_action_group()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.WidgetExt.html#tymethod.insert_action_group)
on the menus attach widget or on any of its parent widgets.

# MenuToolButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.MenuToolButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct MenuToolButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ MenuToolButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuToolButton.html) is a

[that contains a button and a small additional button with an arrow. When clicked, the arrow button pops up a dropdown menu.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ToolItem.html)

`ToolItem`Use [ new()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuToolButton.html#method.new) to create a new

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MenuToolButton.html)

`MenuToolButton`The GtkMenuToolButton implementation of the GtkBuildable interface
supports adding a menu by specifying “menu” as the “type” attribute
of a `<child>` element.

An example for a UI definition fragment with menus:

**⚠️ The following code is in xml ⚠️**

```
<object class="GtkMenuToolButton">
  <child type="menu">
    <object class="GtkMenu"/>
  </child>
</object>
```
