# MessageDialog in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.MessageDialog.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct MessageDialog { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ MessageDialog](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MessageDialog.html) presents a dialog with some message text. It’s simply a
convenience widget; you could construct the equivalent of

[from](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MessageDialog.html)

`MessageDialog`[without too much effort, but](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Dialog.html)

`Dialog`[saves typing.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MessageDialog.html)

`MessageDialog`One difference from [ Dialog](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Dialog.html) is that

[sets the](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MessageDialog.html)

`MessageDialog``property::Window::skip-taskbar-hint` property to [, so that the dialog is hidden from the taskbar by default.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`The easiest way to do a modal message dialog is to use [ DialogExt::run()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DialogExt.html#tymethod.run), though
you can also pass in the

[flag,](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DialogFlags.html#associatedconstant.MODAL)

`DialogFlags::MODAL`[automatically makes the dialog modal and waits for the user to respond to it.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DialogExt.html#tymethod.run)

`DialogExt::run()`[returns when any dialog button is clicked.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DialogExt.html#tymethod.run)

`DialogExt::run()`An example for using a modal dialog:

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
 GtkDialogFlags flags = GTK_DIALOG_DESTROY_WITH_PARENT;
 dialog = gtk_message_dialog_new (parent_window,
                                  flags,
                                  GTK_MESSAGE_ERROR,
                                  GTK_BUTTONS_CLOSE,
                                  "Error reading “%s”: %s",
                                  filename,
                                  g_strerror (errno));
 gtk_dialog_run (GTK_DIALOG (dialog));
 gtk_widget_destroy (dialog);
```
You might do a non-modal [ MessageDialog](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MessageDialog.html) as follows:

An example for a non-modal dialog:

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
 GtkDialogFlags flags = GTK_DIALOG_DESTROY_WITH_PARENT;
 dialog = gtk_message_dialog_new (parent_window,
                                  flags,
                                  GTK_MESSAGE_ERROR,
                                  GTK_BUTTONS_CLOSE,
                                  "Error reading “%s”: %s",
                                  filename,
                                  g_strerror (errno));
 // Destroy the dialog when the user responds to it
 // (e.g. clicks a button)
 g_signal_connect_swapped (dialog, "response",
                           G_CALLBACK (gtk_widget_destroy),
                           dialog);
```
The GtkMessageDialog implementation of the GtkBuildable interface exposes the message area as an internal child with the name “message_area”.

# Misc in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Misc.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Misc { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ Misc](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Misc.html) widget is an abstract widget which is not useful itself, but
is used to derive subclasses which have alignment and padding attributes.

The horizontal and vertical padding attributes allows extra space to be added around the widget.

The horizontal and vertical alignment attributes enable the widget to be positioned within its allocated area. Note that if the widget is added to a container in such a way that it expands automatically to fill its allocated area, the alignment settings will not alter the widget’s position.

Note that the desired effect can in most cases be achieved by using the
`property::Widget::halign`, `property::Widget::valign` and `property::Widget::margin` properties
on the child widget, so GtkMisc should not be used in new code. To reflect
this fact, all [ Misc](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Misc.html) API has been deprecated.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

# ModelButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.ModelButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct ModelButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkModelButton is a button class that can use a `GAction` as its model.
In contrast to [ ToggleButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ToggleButton.html) or

[, which can also be backed by a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html)

`RadioButton``GAction` via the `property::Actionable::action-name` property,
GtkModelButton will adapt its appearance according to the kind of
action it is backed by, and appear either as a plain, check or
radio button.Model buttons are used when popovers from a menu model with
[ Popover::from_model()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Popover.html#method.from_model); they can also be used manually in
a

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PopoverMenu.html)

`PopoverMenu`When the action is specified via the `property::Actionable::action-name`
and `property::Actionable::action-target` properties, the role of the button
(i.e. whether it is a plain, check or radio button) is determined by
the type of the action and doesn’t have to be explicitly specified
with the `property::ModelButton::role` property.

The content of the button is specified by the `property::ModelButton::text`
and `property::ModelButton::icon` properties.

The appearance of model buttons can be influenced with the
`property::ModelButton::centered` and `property::ModelButton::iconic` properties.

Model buttons have built-in support for submenus in [ PopoverMenu](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.PopoverMenu.html).
To make a GtkModelButton that opens a submenu when activated, set
the

`property::ModelButton::menu-name` property. To make a button that goes
back to the parent menu, you should set the `property::ModelButton::inverted`
property to place the submenu indicator at the opposite side.**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
modelbutton
├── <child>
╰── check
```
**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
modelbutton
├── <child>
╰── radio
```
**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
modelbutton
├── <child>
╰── arrow
```
GtkModelButton has a main CSS node with name modelbutton, and a subnode, which will have the name check, radio or arrow, depending on the role of the button and whether it has a menu name set.

The subnode is positioned before or after the content nodes and gets the .left or .right style class, depending on where it is located.

**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
button.model
├── <child>
╰── check
```
Iconic model buttons (see `property::ModelButton::iconic`) change the name of
their main node to button and add a .model style class to it. The indicator
subnode is invisible in this case.

# RadioButton in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.RadioButton.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct RadioButton { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A single radio button performs the same basic function as a [ CheckButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.CheckButton.html),
as its position in the object hierarchy reflects. It is only when multiple
radio buttons are grouped together that they become a different user
interface component in their own right.

Every radio button is a member of some group of radio buttons. When one is
selected, all other radio buttons in the same group are deselected. A
[ RadioButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html) is one way of giving the user a choice from many options.

Radio button widgets are created with [ new()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html#method.new), passing

[as the argument if this is the first radio button in a group. In subsequent calls, the group you wish to add this button to should be passed as an argument. Optionally,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[can be used if you want a text label on the radio button.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html#method.with_label)

`with_label()`Alternatively, when adding widgets to an existing group of radio buttons,
use [ from_widget()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html#method.from_widget) with a

[that already has a group assigned to it. The convenience function](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html)

`RadioButton`[is also provided.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html#method.with_label_from_widget)

`with_label_from_widget()`To retrieve the group a [ RadioButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html) is assigned to, use

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.RadioButtonExt.html#tymethod.group)

`RadioButtonExt::group()`To remove a [ RadioButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html) from one group and make it part of a new one,
use

`gtk_radio_button_set_group()`.The group list does not need to be freed, as each [ RadioButton](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RadioButton.html) will remove
itself and its list item when it is destroyed.

**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
radiobutton
├── radio
╰── <child>
```
A GtkRadioButton with indicator (see [ ToggleButtonExt::set_mode()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.ToggleButtonExt.html#tymethod.set_mode)) has a
main CSS node with name radiobutton and a subnode with name radio.

**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
button.radio
├── radio
╰── <child>
```
A GtkRadioButton without indicator changes the name of its main node to button and adds a .radio style class to it. The subnode is invisible in this case.

**⚠️ The following code is in C ⚠️**

```
void create_radio_buttons (void) {
   GtkWidget *window, *radio1, *radio2, *box, *entry;
   window = gtk_window_new (GTK_WINDOW_TOPLEVEL);
   box = gtk_box_new (GTK_ORIENTATION_VERTICAL, 2);
   gtk_box_set_homogeneous (GTK_BOX (box), TRUE);
   // Create a radio button with a GtkEntry widget
   radio1 = gtk_radio_button_new (NULL);
   entry = gtk_entry_new ();
   gtk_container_add (GTK_CONTAINER (radio1), entry);
   // Create a radio button with a label
   radio2 = gtk_radio_button_new_with_label_from_widget (GTK_RADIO_BUTTON (radio1),
                                                         "I’m the second radio button.");
   // Pack them into a box, then show all the widgets
   gtk_box_pack_start (GTK_BOX (box), radio1);
   gtk_box_pack_start (GTK_BOX (box), radio2);
   gtk_container_add (GTK_CONTAINER (window), box);
   gtk_widget_show_all (window);
   return;
}
```
When an unselected button in the group is clicked the clicked button
receives the `signal::ToggleButton::toggled` signal, as does the previously
selected button.
Inside the `signal::ToggleButton::toggled` handler, [ ToggleButtonExt::is_active()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.ToggleButtonExt.html#tymethod.is_active)
can be used to determine if the button has been selected or deselected.

# NativeDialog in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.NativeDialog.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct NativeDialog { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Native dialogs are platform dialogs that don’t use [ Dialog](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Dialog.html) or

[. They are used in order to integrate better with a platform, by looking the same as other native applications and supporting platform specific features.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Window.html)

`Window`The [ Dialog](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Dialog.html) functions cannot be used on such objects, but we
need a similar API in order to drive them. The

[object is an API that allows you to do this. It allows you to set various common properties on the dialog, as well as show and hide it and get a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.NativeDialog.html)

`NativeDialog``signal::NativeDialog::response` signal when the user finished
with the dialog.There is also a [ NativeDialogExt::run()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.NativeDialogExt.html#tymethod.run) helper that makes it easy
to run any native dialog in a modal way with a recursive mainloop,
similar to

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.DialogExt.html#tymethod.run)

`DialogExt::run()`This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

# Notebook in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Notebook.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Notebook { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ Notebook](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Notebook.html) widget is a

[whose children are pages that can be switched between using tab labels along one edge.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Container.html)

`Container`There are many configuration options for GtkNotebook. Among other
things, you can choose on which edge the tabs appear
(see [ NotebookExt::set_tab_pos()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.NotebookExt.html#tymethod.set_tab_pos)), whether, if there are too many
tabs to fit the notebook should be made bigger or scrolling
arrows added (see

[), and whether there will be a popup menu allowing the users to switch pages. (see](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.NotebookExt.html#tymethod.set_scrollable)

`NotebookExt::set_scrollable()`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.NotebookExt.html#tymethod.popup_enable)

`NotebookExt::popup_enable()`[)](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.NotebookExt.html#tymethod.popup_disable)

`NotebookExt::popup_disable()`The GtkNotebook implementation of the [ Buildable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Buildable.html) interface
supports placing children into tabs by specifying “tab” as the
“type” attribute of a

`<child>` element. Note that the content
of the tab must be created before the tab can be filled.
A tab child can be specified without specifying a `<child>`
type attribute.To add a child widget in the notebooks action area, specify
“action-start” or “action-end” as the “type” attribute of the
`<child>` element.

An example of a UI definition fragment with GtkNotebook:

**⚠️ The following code is in xml ⚠️**

```
<object class="GtkNotebook">
  <child>
    <object class="GtkLabel" id="notebook-content">
      <property name="label">Content</property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child type="tab">
    <object class="GtkLabel" id="notebook-tab">
      <property name="label">Tab</property>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```
**⚠️ The following code is in plain ⚠️**

```
notebook
├── header.top
│   ├── [<action widget>]
│   ├── tabs
│   │   ├── [arrow]
│   │   ├── tab
│   │   │   ╰── <tab label>
┊   ┊   ┊
│   │   ├── tab[.reorderable-page]
│   │   │   ╰── <tab label>
│   │   ╰── [arrow]
│   ╰── [<action widget>]
│
╰── stack
    ├── <child>
    ┊
    ╰── <child>
```
GtkNotebook has a main CSS node with name notebook, a subnode with name header and below that a subnode with name tabs which contains one subnode per tab with name tab.

If action widgets are present, their CSS nodes are placed next to the tabs node. If the notebook is scrollable, CSS nodes with name arrow are placed as first and last child of the tabs node.

The main node gets the .frame style class when the notebook
has a border (see [ NotebookExt::set_show_border()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.NotebookExt.html#tymethod.set_show_border)).

The header node gets one of the style class .top, .bottom, .left or .right, depending on where the tabs are placed. For reorderable pages, the tab node gets the .reorderable-page class.

A tab node gets the .dnd style class while it is moved with drag-and-drop.

The nodes are always arranged from left-to-right, regarldess of text direction.

# OffscreenWindow in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.OffscreenWindow.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct OffscreenWindow { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkOffscreenWindow is strictly intended to be used for obtaining
snapshots of widgets that are not part of a normal widget hierarchy.
Since [ OffscreenWindow](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.OffscreenWindow.html) is a toplevel widget you cannot obtain
snapshots of a full window with it since you cannot pack a toplevel
widget in another toplevel.

The idea is to take a widget and manually set the state of it,
add it to a GtkOffscreenWindow and then retrieve the snapshot
as a [ cairo::Surface](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/cairo/surface/struct.Surface.html) or

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/0.15/docs/gdk_pixbuf/auto/pixbuf/struct.Pixbuf.html)

`gdk_pixbuf::Pixbuf`GtkOffscreenWindow derives from [ Window](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Window.html) only as an implementation
detail. Applications should not use any API specific to

[to operate on this object. It should be treated as a](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[that has no parent widget.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Bin.html)

`Bin`When contained offscreen widgets are redrawn, GtkOffscreenWindow
will emit a `signal::Widget::damage-event` signal.

# Orientable in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Orientable.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Orientable { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ Orientable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Orientable.html) interface is implemented by all widgets that can be
oriented horizontally or vertically. Historically, such widgets have been
realized as subclasses of a common base class (e.g

[/](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Box.html)

`Box``GtkHBox`/`GtkVBox`
or [/](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Scale.html)

`Scale``GtkHScale`/`GtkVScale`). [is more flexible in that it allows the orientation to be changed at runtime, allowing the widgets to “flip”.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Orientable.html)

`Orientable`[ Orientable](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Orientable.html) was introduced in GTK+ 2.16.

# Overlay in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/struct.Overlay.html

`#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Overlay { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

GtkOverlay is a container which contains a single main child, on top
of which it can place “overlay” widgets. The position of each overlay
widget is determined by its `property::Widget::halign` and `property::Widget::valign`
properties. E.g. a widget with both alignments set to [ Align::Start](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Align.html#variant.Start)
will be placed at the top left corner of the GtkOverlay container,
whereas an overlay with halign set to

[and valign set to](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Align.html#variant.Center)

`Align::Center`[will be placed a the bottom edge of the GtkOverlay, horizontally centered. The position can be adjusted by setting the margin properties of the child to non-zero values.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Align.html#variant.End)

`Align::End`More complicated placement of overlays is possible by connecting
to the `signal::Overlay::get-child-position` signal.

An overlay’s minimum and natural sizes are those of its main child. The sizes of overlay children are not considered when measuring these preferred sizes.

The GtkOverlay implementation of the GtkBuildable interface
supports placing a child as an overlay by specifying “overlay” as
the “type” attribute of a `<child>` element.

GtkOverlay has a single CSS node with the name “overlay”. Overlay children whose alignments cause them to be positioned at an edge get the style classes “.left”, “.right”, “.top”, and/or “.bottom” according to their position.

# Align in gtk - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk3-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk/enum.Align.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum Align {
    Fill,
    Start,
    End,
    Center,
    Baseline,
    // some variants omitted
}
```

## Expand description

Controls how a widget deals with extra space in a single (x or y)
dimension.

Alignment only matters if the widget receives a “too large” allocation,
for example if you packed the widget with the `property::Widget::expand`
flag inside a `Box`

Note that in horizontal context `Start``End`

GTK_ALIGN_BASELINE support for it is optional for containers and widgets, and
it is only supported for vertical alignment. When its not supported by
a child or a container it is treated as `Fill`

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.
